title.zh: 卷三百十七 列傳第七十六 邵亢 馮京 錢惟演
title.en: Volume 317 Biographies 76: Shao Kang, Feng Jing, Qian Weiyan
title.raw: 卷三百十七 列傳第七十六 邵亢 馮京 錢惟演 Volume 317 Biographies 76: Shao Kang, Feng Jing, Qian Weiyan

sentences.zh: 邵亢從父:必 馮京 錢惟演從弟:易 易子:彥遠 明逸 諸孫 諸孫:景諶 勰 即

translations.literal: Shao Kang, father's cousin: Bi; Feng Jing; Qian Weiyan, younger cousin: Yi; Yi's sons: Yanyuan, Mingyi; grandsons; grandsons: Jingchen, Xie, Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Figures treated in this chapter include Shao Kang's father's cousin Bi, Feng Jing, and Qian Weiyan's younger cousin Yi, whose sons were Yanyuan and Mingyi and whose grandsons were Jingchen, Xie, and Ji.

sentences.zh: 邵亢，字興宗，丹陽人。

translations.literal: Shao Kang, styled Xingzong, was a man of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Kang, whose style name was Xingzong, came from Danyang.

sentences.zh: 幼聰發過人，方十歲，日誦書五千言。

translations.literal: In youth his intelligence surpassed others; at just ten years old he could recite five thousand characters of text per day.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy his brilliance outstripped his peers; by the age of ten he was reciting five thousand characters of text each day.

sentences.zh: 賦詩豪縱，鄉先生見者皆驚偉之。

translations.literal: His fu poetry was bold and unrestrained, and village teachers who saw him were all startled and admired his greatness.
translations.idiomatic: His fu verse was bold and free, and every local teacher who met him was struck by his extraordinary promise.

sentences.zh: 再試開封，當第一，以賦失韻，弗取。

translations.literal: On his second Kaifeng examination he would have ranked first, but because his fu violated the rhyme scheme he was not selected.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the Kaifeng examination a second time he would have placed first, but a rhyme fault in his fu cost him the degree.

sentences.zh: 范仲淹舉亢茂才異等，時布衣被召者十四人，試崇政殿，獨亢策入等，除建康軍節度推官。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan recommended Kang as a student of outstanding talent and special distinction; at the time fourteen commoners were summoned, and when tested in the Chongzheng Hall only Kang's policy essay passed into the graded ranks; he was appointed military pushan of the Jiankang Army circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan nominated him for the "outstanding talent, special distinction" category. Fourteen commoners were summoned to court; examined in the Chongzheng Hall, Kang alone qualified with his policy essay and was made pushan on the Jiankang circuit staff.

sentences.zh: 或言所對策字少，不應式，宰相張士遜與之姻家，故得預選，遂報罷。

translations.literal: Someone said his policy essay had too few characters and did not meet the format, and that because Grand Councilor Zhang Shisun was related to him by marriage he had been allowed into the selection; his appointment was then revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Critics claimed his essay was too short to meet the rules and that he had only been shortlisted because Grand Councilor Zhang Shisun was a kinsman by marriage; the appointment was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 而士遜子實娶它邵，與亢同姓耳。

translations.literal: In fact Shisun's son Shi had married another person surnamed Shao, who merely shared the same surname as Kang.
translations.idiomatic: In truth Zhang's son had married a different Shao family; the connection was nothing more than a shared surname.

sentences.zh: 士遜既不能與直，亢亦不自言。

translations.literal: Since Shisun could not speak frankly about it, Kang also did not speak of it himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shisun could not set the record straight, and Kang likewise kept silent.

sentences.zh: 趙元吳叛，亢言：「用兵在於擇將，今天下久不知戰，而所任多儒臣，未必能應變。

translations.literal: When Zhao Yuanhao rebelled, Kang said: "The use of troops lies in choosing generals; the realm has long been unaccustomed to war, yet those appointed are mostly Confucian officials who may not be able to respond to changing circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yuanhao rose in rebellion, Kang argued: "Warfare depends on choosing the right commanders. The empire has not fought in ages, yet we keep appointing scholar-officials who may not adapt when circumstances shift.

sentences.zh: 武人得長一軍，又已老，詎能身先矢石哉？

translations.literal: When a military man is allowed to command an army, he is already old—how can he lead in person before arrows and stones?
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers who do win field commands are already elderly—how can they lead from the front under fire?

sentences.zh: 間起故家恩幸子弟，彼安識攻守之計？

translations.literal: From time to time scions of old families favored by the throne are raised up—how would they know plans for attack and defense?
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes we elevate pampered sons of great houses—what do they know of siege and assault?

sentences.zh: 況將與卒素不相附，又亡堅甲利兵之御。

translations.literal: Moreover, generals and soldiers are not naturally attached to one another, and there is no defense of stout armor and sharp weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Generals and rank-and-file seldom trust one another, and we lack the hard armor and keen weapons needed for defense.

sentences.zh: 此不待兩軍相當，而勝敗之機，固已形矣。」

translations.literal: This does not wait for the two armies to meet; the moment of victory and defeat is already taking shape."
translations.idiomatic: We need not even wait for the armies to clash—the outcome is already plain."

sentences.zh: 因獻《兵說》十篇。

translations.literal: He thereupon presented ten chapters of "Discourse on Warfare."
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted ten chapters of his Discourse on Warfare.

sentences.zh: 契丹遣使賀乾元節，未至，仁宗崩。

translations.literal: The Khitan sent envoys to congratulate the Qianyuan Festival; before they arrived, Emperor Renzong died.
translations.idiomatic: Liao dispatched envoys for the Qianyuan birthday celebration, but before they arrived Emperor Renzong had died.

sentences.zh: 議者謂宜卻，或欲俟其及國門而諭使之還，亢請令奉書至柩前，使見嗣君。

translations.literal: Discussants said they should be turned back, or wished to wait until they reached the capital gate and then instruct them to return; Kang asked that they be allowed to present their letter before the coffin and see the heir.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued the envoys should be refused outright, others that they should be met at the gate and sent home; Kang urged that they be allowed to present their credentials before the bier and meet the new emperor.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 選為潁王府翊善，加直史館。

translations.literal: He was selected as tutor to the Prince of Ying's household and given concurrent appointment in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He was made tutor to the Prince of Ying and given a concurrent post in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 召對群玉殿，英宗訪以世事，稱之曰：「學士真國器也。」

translations.literal: Summoned to audience in the Hall of Gathered Jade, Emperor Yingzong questioned him on affairs of state and praised him, saying: "Academician, you are truly a vessel of the state."
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to the Hall of Gathered Jade, Emperor Yingzong questioned him on public affairs and declared, "Academician, you are a true pillar of the realm."

sentences.zh: 擢同修起居注。

translations.literal: He was promoted to co-compiler of the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to co-compiler of the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 建言：「陛下初政，欲治國者先齊家，潁王且授室，願採用古昏禮。

translations.literal: He submitted advice: "Your Majesty's government is new; one who would govern the state must first put the household in order. The Prince of Ying is about to take a wife; I hope the ancient wedding rites may be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: He advised: "At the start of your reign you must put your own house in order before you can govern the realm. The Prince of Ying is about to marry; I urge that the ancient wedding ceremonies be followed.

sentences.zh: 公主下降，不宜厭舅姑之尊。」

translations.literal: When a princess marries down, it is not fitting to demean the dignity of her parents-in-law."
translations.idiomatic: When an imperial princess marries a subject, her in-laws should not be made to humble themselves before her."

sentences.zh: 帝深納之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the advice to heart.

sentences.zh: 他日，諭王曰：「以翊善端直樸厚，輟為諫官矣。」

translations.literal: Another day he instructed the prince: "Because the tutor is upright, plain, and sincere, I have transferred him to be a remonstrance official."
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion he told the prince, "Your tutor is so upright and steadfast that I have moved him to the remonstrance bureau."

sentences.zh: 王出道帝語，遂以知制誥知諫院。

translations.literal: The prince went out and reported the emperor's words, and Kang was thereupon made drafter of edicts and head of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The prince repeated the emperor's remark outside court, and Kang was appointed drafter of edicts with charge of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 東宮建，為右庶子。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Palace was established, he became Right Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's household.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent's household was formally established, he was made its right vice director.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，遷龍圖閣直學士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong acceded, Kang was transferred to academician ex officio of the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong came to the throne, Kang was promoted to academician ex officio of the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 有譖之者曰：「先帝大漸時，亢嘗建垂簾之議。」

translations.literal: Someone slandered him, saying: "When the late emperor was gravely ill, Kang once proposed a regency behind the curtain."
translations.idiomatic: A detractor claimed that during the late emperor's final illness Kang had urged a regency behind the curtain."

sentences.zh: 御史吳申即論之。

translations.literal: Censor Wu Shen immediately memorialized against him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wu Shen promptly impeached him on that charge.

sentences.zh: 帝知其妄，置不問。

translations.literal: The emperor knew it was false and set the matter aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew the charge was baseless and ignored it.

sentences.zh: 亢自訴曰：「方先帝不豫，群臣莫得進見，臣無由面陳，必有章奏。

translations.literal: Kang pleaded in his own defense: "When the late emperor was unwell, the ministers could not gain audience; I had no means to speak face to face—there must be a memorial on record.
translations.idiomatic: Kang rebutted the charge himself: "When the late emperor fell ill, none of us could see him. I could only have spoken through a memorial—search the palace archives.

sentences.zh: 乞索之禁中，若得之，臣當伏誅；

translations.literal: I beg that it be sought within the palace; if it is found, I should submit to execution;
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the inner archives be searched; if such a document exists, I deserve death;

sentences.zh: 不然，則讒臣者，豈宜但已，願下獄考實。」

translations.literal: otherwise, should the slanderer of me simply be let off? I wish to be imprisoned so the facts may be examined."
translations.idiomatic: and if not, the man who slandered me should not walk free—I ask to be jailed while the truth is established."

sentences.zh: 帝不許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 時待制以上為帥、守，每他徙必遷職秩，亢請未滿兩歲者勿推恩。

translations.literal: At the time, when officials of associate academician rank and above served as commanders or prefects, each transfer brought a promotion in rank; Kang requested that those who had not completed two years should not receive such favors.
translations.idiomatic: At the time every transfer of a circuit commander or prefect at associate-academician rank or above brought an automatic promotion; Kang urged that no such favor be granted unless two years had been served.

sentences.zh: 王陶劾韓琦，吳奎與之辨。

translations.literal: Wang Tao impeached Han Qi, and Wu Kui argued on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tao impeached Han Qi, and Wu Kui defended him.

sentences.zh: 亢詆奎所言顛倒，失大臣體，蓋欲亻並撼琦。

translations.literal: Kang denounced Kui's words as inverted and unbecoming a great minister, presumably intending to join forces and shake Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Kang attacked Kui's defense as incoherent and unworthy of a chief minister, evidently hoping to combine with others and bring Qi down.

sentences.zh: 琦與奎竟同日去。

translations.literal: Qi and Kui in the end left office on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: In the end both Qi and Kui left office on the same day.

sentences.zh: 進樞密直學士、知開封府。

translations.literal: He was advanced to academician ex officio of the Bureau of Military Affairs and made prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to academician ex officio of the Bureau of Military Affairs and appointed prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 亢遇事敏密，吏操辭牘至前，皆反覆閱之。

translations.literal: Kang was quick and thorough in handling affairs; when clerks brought documents before him he read each one over repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Kang handled business with quick, meticulous care, reading every document a clerk placed before him again and again.

sentences.zh: 人或以為勞，亢曰：「決是非於須臾，正當爾。

translations.literal: Some thought this laborious; Kang said: "To decide right and wrong in an instant—this is exactly what one should do.
translations.idiomatic: Some thought this excessive; Kang replied, "When right and wrong must be decided in a moment, this is exactly what is required.

sentences.zh: 初雖煩，後乃省也。」

translations.literal: At first it is troublesome, but afterward one saves effort."
translations.idiomatic: It is tedious at first, but in the end it saves work."

sentences.zh: 籍里閭惡少年與吏之廢停者，一有所犯，皆遷處之，畿下斗訟為之衰止。

translations.literal: He registered neighborhood ruffians and dismissed or idle clerks; on any offense they were all relocated, and brawling and litigation in the capital region declined and ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He kept registers of neighborhood thugs and idle or dismissed clerks and banished anyone who offended again; quarrels and lawsuits around the capital dwindled away.

sentences.zh: 拜樞密副使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 夏人誘殺知保安軍楊定，朝廷謀西討。

translations.literal: The Xia people lured and killed Yang Ding, military commander of Bao'an, and the court planned a western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut lured and killed Yang Ding, commander of Bao'an Army, and the court began planning a punitive expedition westward.

sentences.zh: 亢曰：「天下財力殫屈，未宜用兵，唯當降意撫納，俟不順命，則師出有名矣。」

translations.literal: Kang said: "The realm's wealth and strength are exhausted; troops should not yet be used. One should only lower one's stance and soothe and accept them; when they disobey orders, then the army may march with a righteous name."
translations.idiomatic: Kang argued: "The empire's resources are spent—we should not fight yet. Lower our tone, offer conciliation, and wait until they defy us; then we march with justice on our side."

sentences.zh: 因條上其事。

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted a detailed memorial on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He followed with a detailed memorial laying out his plan.

sentences.zh: 詔報之曰：「中國民力，大事也。

translations.literal: An edict replied to him: "The strength of the people of China is a great matter.
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied: "The strength of our people is a matter of the highest importance.

sentences.zh: 兵興之後，不無倍率，人心一搖，安危所系。

translations.literal: After war is raised there is inevitably doubling of levies; if popular sentiment wavers once, safety and peril are bound up in it.
translations.idiomatic: Once war begins, taxes inevitably multiply; a single shift in public morale touches the fate of the realm.

sentences.zh: 今動自我始，先違信誓，契丹聞之，將不期而自合，茲朕所深憂者。

translations.literal: Now if we move first, we violate our sworn faith beforehand; when the Khitan hear of it they will unite without being summoned—this is what I deeply fear.
translations.idiomatic: If we strike first we break faith before anyone else does; the Khitan will hear of it and rally against us without prompting—that is my deepest worry.

sentences.zh: 當悉如卿計。」

translations.literal: We should entirely follow your plan."
translations.idiomatic: We shall follow your counsel in full."

sentences.zh: 未幾，夏主諒祚死，國人執殺定者來請和。

translations.literal: Before long the Xia ruler Liangzuo died, and the Xia people seized the man who had killed Ding and came to sue for peace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Tangut ruler Liangzuo died, and his subjects handed over Ding's killer and sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 或欲乘此更取塞門地，亢以為幸人之喪，非義也，乃止。

translations.literal: Some wished to take advantage of this to seize more border passes; Kang held that to profit from another's bereavement was not righteous, and the plan was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged seizing more frontier passes while the Tangut mourned; Kang called it unrighteous to profit from a neighbor's grief, and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 從父 必

translations.literal: Father's cousin: Bi
translations.idiomatic: His father's cousin Bi

sentences.zh: 必字不疑。

translations.literal: Bi, styled Buyi.
translations.idiomatic: Bi, whose style name was Buyi.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，為上元主簿。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as registrar of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree and served as registrar of Shangyuan county.

sentences.zh: 國子監立石經，必善篆隸，召充直講。

translations.literal: When the Directorate of Education erected the stone classics, Bi was skilled in seal and clerical script and was summoned to serve as lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: When the Directorate of Education carved the stone classics, Bi's mastery of seal and clerical script won him appointment as a lecturer.

sentences.zh: 選為《唐書》編修官。

translations.literal: He was selected as a compiler of the Book of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: He was chosen as a compiler of the Book of Tang.

sentences.zh: 必以史出眾手，非古人撰述之體，辭不就。

translations.literal: Bi held that a history produced by many hands was not in the manner of ancient authorship and declined the post.
translations.idiomatic: Bi refused, arguing that a history written by committee was not how the ancients composed and he would not take part.

sentences.zh: 進集賢校理、同知太常禮院。

translations.literal: He was advanced to collator in the Hall of Assembled Talents and concurrent vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to collator in the Hall of Assembled Talents and made vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 天子且親祠，執事者習禮壇下。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was about to sacrifice in person, and the officiants practiced the rites below the altar.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was to perform the sacrifices in person, and the ritual officers rehearsed the ceremonies at the altar.

sentences.zh: 必言：「《周官·大宗伯》：『凡王之禱祠，肄儀為位。』

translations.literal: Bi said: "In the Zhou Offices, Grand Invocator: 'For all the king's prayer sacrifices, drill the ritual and set the positions.'
translations.idiomatic: Bi objected: "The Zhou Offices, Grand Invocator chapter, says: 'For all the king's prayer sacrifices, rehearse the ceremony and mark the positions.'

sentences.zh: 鄭康成釋云：『若今肄司徒府。』

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan explains: 'As when one drills today in the Minister of Education's office.'"
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan glosses this as 'like rehearsing today in the Minister of Education's office.'"

sentences.zh: 古禮如此。

translations.literal: Ancient ritual was thus.
translations.idiomatic: That was ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 今即祠所習之，為不敬。」

translations.literal: To practice now at the very site of sacrifice is disrespectful."
translations.idiomatic: Rehearsing on the sacred ground itself is disrespectful."

sentences.zh: 乃徙於尚書省。

translations.literal: The rehearsal was therefore moved to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The rehearsal was moved to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 張貴妃受冊，禮官議命婦入賀儀未決，或曰：「妃為修媛時，命婦已不敢亢禮，況今日乎？」

translations.literal: When Consort Zhang received investiture, ritual officials debated the ceremony for titled ladies entering to congratulate, without reaching a decision; someone said: "When the consort was a Cultivated Lady, titled ladies already did not dare match her in ritual precedence—how much less today?"
translations.idiomatic: When Consort Zhang was invested, ritualists could not agree how titled ladies should offer congratulations. Some argued that even when she had been only a Cultivated Lady, noblewomen had not dared claim equal precedence—how much less now?"

sentences.zh: 必曰：「宮省事秘不可知。

translations.literal: Bi said: "Palace affairs are secret and cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: Bi replied: "Inner-palace arrangements are unknowable from outside.

sentences.zh: 既下有司議，惟有外一品南省上事百官班見之儀，然禮無不答。」

translations.literal: Since the matter has been sent down for the offices to deliberate, there is only the ceremony for first-rank ladies outside the palace presenting matters at the southern ministry with the full official corps in attendance—but in ritual there is none that goes unanswered."
translations.idiomatic: The question is now before the ministries, and the only precedent is for first-rank ladies outside the palace to present congratulations with the full court in attendance—yet ritual always demands a response."

sentences.zh: 眾議乃定。

translations.literal: The collective deliberation was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: On that basis the court settled the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 出知常州，召為開封府推官。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as prefect of Changzhou and was recalled as investigating officer of the Kaifeng prefectural government.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Changzhou, then was recalled as an investigating officer in the Kaifeng prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 坐在常州日杖人至死，責監邵武稅，然杖者實不死。

translations.literal: He was convicted because in Changzhou he had beaten a man to death with the staff; he was punished by supervision of the Shaowu tax office, yet the man beaten had in fact not died.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished for having flogged a man to death while in Changzhou and was demoted to oversee the Shaowu tax office, though the man he flogged had not actually died.

sentences.zh: 久之，知高郵軍，提點淮南刑獄，為京西轉運使。

translations.literal: After a long while he became military prefect of Gaoyou, intendant of Huainan judicial affairs, and transport commissioner of the Jingxi circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made military prefect of Gaoyou, intendant of Huainan judicial affairs, and transport commissioner on the Jingxi circuit.

sentences.zh: 必居官震厲風采，始至郡，惟一赴宴集；

translations.literal: In office Bi was stern and imposing in bearing; when he first arrived in a prefecture he attended only one banquet gathering;
translations.idiomatic: Bi governed with stern, commanding presence; on first reaching a prefecture he accepted only one banquet;

sentences.zh: 行部，但一受酒食之饋。

translations.literal: on inspection tours he accepted only one gift of food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: on circuit inspection he took only one offering of food and drink.

sentences.zh: 以為數會聚則人情狎，多受饋則不能行事，非使者體也。

translations.literal: He held that frequent gatherings made feelings familiar and that receiving many gifts meant one could not conduct affairs—this was not the manner of an envoy.
translations.idiomatic: He believed that frequent socializing bred familiarity and that too many gifts made it impossible to govern—neither befitted a touring commissioner.

sentences.zh: 入修起居注、知制誥。

translations.literal: He entered the capital to compile the Veritable Records and serve as drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court to compile the Veritable Records and serve as drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 雄州種木道上，契丹遣人夜伐去，又數漁界河中。

translations.literal: On the tree-planted road at Xiongzhou the Khitan sent men by night to cut the trees down, and they also fished repeatedly in the border river.
translations.idiomatic: Along the tree-lined road at Xiongzhou, Liao sent men to cut the trees down by night and repeatedly fished in the border river.

sentences.zh: 事聞，命必往使，必以理折契丹，屈之。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Bi was ordered to go as envoy; with reason he refuted the Khitan and bent them to submission.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached court, Bi was sent as envoy; he overwhelmed the Khitan with argument until they yielded.

sentences.zh: 還，知諫院。

translations.literal: On his return he was made head of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he headed the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 編《仁宗御集》成，遷寶文閣直學士、權三司使，加龍圖閣學士、知成都。

translations.literal: When the compilation of the Collected Writings of Emperor Renzong was completed, he was transferred to academician ex officio of the Hall of Treasured Culture, acting commissioner of the Three Fiscal Commissions, and given the additional titles of academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: After completing the Collected Writings of Emperor Renzong, he was made academician ex officio of the Hall of Treasured Culture and acting commissioner of the Three Fiscal Commissions, then given the additional posts of Dragon Diagram academician and prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 卒於道，年六十四。

translations.literal: He died on the road at the age of sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the journey at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 遣中使護其喪歸。

translations.literal: The court sent a palace envoy to escort his coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: The court dispatched a palace envoy to escort his remains home.

sentences.zh: 馮京，字當世，鄂州江夏人。

translations.literal: Feng Jing, styled Dangshi, was a man of Jiangxia in Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jing, whose style name was Dangshi, came from Jiangxia in Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 少雋邁不群，舉進士，自鄉舉、禮部以至廷試，皆第一。

translations.literal: In youth he was brilliant and stood apart from the crowd; he passed the jinshi examination, and from the provincial test through the Ministry of Rites to the palace examination he ranked first in every stage.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was brilliant and unconventional. He took the jinshi degree and placed first at every stage—from the provincial examination through the Ministry of Rites to the palace test.

sentences.zh: 時猶未娶，張堯佐方負宮掖勢，欲妻以女。

translations.literal: He had not yet married; Zhang Yaozuo was then wielding power in the palace quarters and wished to give him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He was still unmarried when Zhang Yaozuo, then powerful in the inner palace, sought to marry his daughter to him.

sentences.zh: 擁至其家，束之以金帶，曰：「此上意也。」

translations.literal: They hustled him to Zhang's house, bound a gold belt on him, and said: "This is the emperor's wish."
translations.idiomatic: They dragged him to Zhang's house, buckled a gold belt on him, and declared, "This is the emperor's wish."

sentences.zh: 頃之，宮中持酒殽來，直出奩具目示之。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward palace attendants brought wine and food, and straightway produced the trousseau list and showed it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon palace servants arrived with wine and food and produced the dowry inventory for him to see.

sentences.zh: 京笑不視，力辭。

translations.literal: Jing laughed and would not look, firmly declining.
translations.idiomatic: Jing laughed and refused to look, steadfastly declining the match.

sentences.zh: 出守將作監丞、通判荊南軍府事。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as vice director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and as administrative assistant of the Jingnan military commission.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital as vice director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and administrative assistant on the Jingnan military staff.

sentences.zh: 還，直集賢院、判吏部南曹，同修起居注。

translations.literal: On his return he was attached to the Hall of Assembled Talents, served as judge of the southern bureau of the Ministry of Personnel, and co-compiled the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was attached to the Hall of Assembled Talents, judged cases in the Ministry of Personnel's southern bureau, and co-compiled the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 吳充以論溫成皇后追冊事，出知高郵，京疏充言是，不當黜。

translations.literal: Wu Chong was sent out to Gaoyou for memorializing on the posthumous enfeoffment of Empress Wen Cheng; Jing memorialized that Chong was right and should not be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chong was banished to Gaoyou for opposing the posthumous ennoblement of Empress Wen Cheng; Jing memorialized that Chong was right and should not have been punished.

sentences.zh: 劉沆請亻並斥京，仁宗曰：「京亦何罪？」

translations.literal: Liu Hong asked to have Jing driven out together with others; Emperor Renzong said: "What crime has Jing committed?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong urged that Jing be expelled along with others; Emperor Renzong asked, "What has Jing done wrong?"

sentences.zh: 但解其記注，旋復之。

translations.literal: He only removed him from compiling the Veritable Records, and soon restored him.
translations.idiomatic: He merely removed him from the Veritable Records post and soon restored him.

sentences.zh: 試知制誥。

translations.literal: He was tried out as drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 避婦父富弼當國嫌，拜龍圖閣待制、知揚州。

translations.literal: To avoid the suspicion of his father-in-law Fu Bi holding power at court, he was appointed awaiting draft in the Dragon Diagram Hall and made prefect of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: To avoid the appearance of favoritism while his father-in-law Fu Bi led the government, he was made awaiting draft in the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 改江寧府，以翰林侍讀學士召還，糾察在京刑獄。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Jiangning prefecture, then recalled as Hanlin academician reader and charged with investigating capital criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Jiangning, then recalled as Hanlin academician reader to investigate criminal cases in the capital.

sentences.zh: 為翰林學士、知開封府。

translations.literal: He became Hanlin academician and prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Hanlin academician and prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 數月不詣丞相府，韓琦語弼，以京為傲。

translations.literal: For months he did not call at the chief councilor's residence; Han Qi told Fu Bi that he considered Jing arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: For months he never called on the chief councilor; Han Qi told Fu Bi that Jing was being arrogant.

sentences.zh: 弼使往見琦，京曰：「公為宰相，從官不妄造請，乃所以為公重，非傲也。」

translations.literal: Bi sent someone to call on Qi; Jing said, "As chief councilor, your attendant officials do not pay visits without cause—that is how they uphold your dignity; it is not arrogance."
translations.idiomatic: Bi sent an envoy to see Qi; Jing explained, "As chief councilor, your attendants do not call without good reason—that is how they preserve your standing, not out of arrogance."

sentences.zh: 出安撫陝西，請城古渭，通西羌唃氏，畀木征官，以斷夏人右臂。

translations.literal: When he went out as pacification commissioner of Shaanxi, he requested that Guwei be fortified, contact be opened with the Western Qiang Gusiluo, and Mu Zheng be granted an official title, so as to sever the Xia people's right arm.
translations.idiomatic: After he was sent out as pacification commissioner of Shaanxi, he urged fortifying Guwei, reaching the Western Qiang Gusiluo, and conferring office on Mu Zheng in order to cut off the Tangut right flank.

sentences.zh: 除端明殿學士、知太原府。

translations.literal: He was appointed academician of the Hall of Manifest Brightness and made prefect of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made academician of the Hall of Manifest Brightness and prefect of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，復為翰林學士，改御史中丞。

translations.literal: When Shenzong acceded, he was again made Hanlin academician and transferred to vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong came to the throne, he was again appointed Hanlin academician and promoted to vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 王安石為政，京論其更張失當，累數千百言，安石指為邪說，請黜之。

translations.literal: When Wang Anshi held power, Jing argued that his reforms were misguided, accumulating several thousand words; Anshi denounced this as heterodox doctrine and requested his dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wang Anshi's administration, Jing wrote thousands of words arguing that the new policies were mistaken; Anshi labeled the views heterodox and asked that he be removed.

sentences.zh: 帝以為可用，擢樞密副使。

translations.literal: The emperor considered him usable and promoted him to vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor found him still useful and promoted him to vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 河東麟、府、豐三州，城壘兵械不治，官吏皆受譴。

translations.literal: In the three prefectures of Lin, Fu, and Feng in Hedong, fortifications and weapons were not maintained, and officials were all punished.
translations.idiomatic: In Hedong's Lin, Fu, and Feng prefectures, city walls and armaments had fallen into neglect, and the responsible officials were all censured.

sentences.zh: 京以先帥本道，上章自劾曰：「使諸路帥臣，知其雖一時脫去，後能僥竊名位者，猶必行法，將不敢復偷惰曠職。」

translations.literal: Jing, having previously commanded this circuit, submitted a memorial impeaching himself, saying, "If circuit commanders know that even those who temporarily escape punishment but later steal back position by luck will still have the law applied, they will not dare again to be lazy and neglect duty."
translations.idiomatic: Jing, who had once commanded the circuit himself, memorialized to impeach himself, saying, "If frontier commanders see that even men who slip away for a time but later claw their way back into office will still be punished, they will not dare again to neglect their duties."

sentences.zh: 優詔不聽。

translations.literal: An edict of grace declined to accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a gracious edict refusing to accept his resignation.

sentences.zh: 進參知政事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 數與安石論辨，又薦劉分攵、蘇軾掌外製。

translations.literal: He repeatedly debated with Anshi, and also recommended Liu Chang and Su Shi to handle external edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He argued repeatedly with Anshi and also recommended Liu Chang and Su Shi to draft external edicts.

sentences.zh: 安石令保甲養馬，京謂必不可行。

translations.literal: Anshi ordered the baojia system to raise horses; Jing said it absolutely could not be implemented.
translations.idiomatic: When Anshi ordered the baojia militia to raise horses, Jing declared the plan utterly unworkable.

sentences.zh: 會選人鄭俠上書言時政，薦京可相，呂惠卿因是譖京與俠通，罷知亳州。

translations.literal: When the examination candidate Zheng Xia submitted a memorial on current affairs recommending Jing for prime minister, Lü Huiqing used this to slander Jing as colluding with Xia, and he was dismissed to be prefect of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the candidate Zheng Xia memorialized on current affairs and recommended Jing as chief minister, Lü Huiqing seized on this to accuse Jing of collusion with Xia, and Jing was demoted to prefect of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以資政殿學士知渭州。

translations.literal: Before long, as academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance he was made prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward he was appointed academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and prefect of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 茂州夷叛，徙知成都府。

translations.literal: When the Yi of Maozhou rebelled, he was transferred to be prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribes of Maozhou rose in revolt, he was transferred to serve as prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 蕃部何丹方寇雞粽關，聞京兵至，請降。

translations.literal: The tribal chieftain He Dan was raiding Jiguan Pass; upon learning Jing's troops had arrived, he requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal leader He Dan was attacking Jiguan Pass, but when he heard that Jing's forces had arrived, he asked to submit.

sentences.zh: 議者遂欲盪其巢窟，京請於朝，為禁侵掠，給稼器，餉糧食，使之歸。

translations.literal: Discussants then wanted to wipe out their nests; Jing petitioned the court to forbid raids, supply farming tools, provide food, and let them return home.
translations.idiomatic: Some at court then wanted to destroy their settlements outright; Jing asked the throne to forbid pillaging, supply farm implements and grain, and allow the people to return home.

sentences.zh: 夷人喜，爭出犬豕割血受盟，願世世為漢藩。

translations.literal: The Yi were pleased; they vied to bring out dogs and pigs, cut blood for a covenant, and vowed to be Han vassals for generations.
translations.idiomatic: The tribesmen rejoiced, vying to bring out dogs and pigs for blood-oath ceremonies and pledging to remain Han subjects for generations.

sentences.zh: 惠卿告安石罪，發其私書，有曰「勿令齊年知」，齊年謂京也，與安石同年生。

translations.literal: Huiqing reported Anshi's crimes and exposed his private letters, which included the phrase "Do not let Tongnian know"; Tongnian meant Jing, who was born in the same year as Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: Huiqing denounced Anshi and revealed his private letters, one of which read, "Do not let Tongnian know"—Tongnian being Jing, who shared Anshi's birth year.

sentences.zh: 帝以安石為欺，復召京知樞密院。

translations.literal: The emperor considered Anshi deceitful and recalled Jing to head the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Believing Anshi had deceived him, the emperor recalled Jing to direct the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 京以疾未至，帝中夕呼左右語曰：「適夢馮京入朝，甚慰人意。」

translations.literal: Jing, ill, had not yet arrived; at midnight the emperor called his attendants and said, "I just dreamed of Feng Jing entering court—it greatly reassured me."
translations.idiomatic: Jing was ill and had not yet reached the capital; in the middle of the night the emperor summoned his attendants and said, "I have just dreamed of Feng Jing coming to court, and it greatly comforted me."

sentences.zh: 乃賜京詔，有「渴想儀刑，不忘夢寐」之語。

translations.literal: He then granted Jing an edict with the words "longing for your exemplary conduct, never forgetting you even in dreams."
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Jing an edict containing the phrase, "I thirst for your example and do not forget you even in sleep."

sentences.zh: 及入見，首以所夢告焉。

translations.literal: When Jing came for an audience, the emperor first told him of the dream.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing arrived for an audience, the emperor told him of the dream at once.

sentences.zh: 頃之，以觀文殿學士知河陽。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, as academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture he was made prefect of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture and prefect of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 哲宗即位，拜保寧軍節度使、知大名府，又改鎮彰德。

translations.literal: When Zhezong acceded, he was appointed military commissioner of Baoning Army and prefect of Daming, then transferred to command Zhangde.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong came to the throne, he was appointed military commissioner of the Baoning Army and prefect of Daming, then transferred to command Zhangde.

sentences.zh: 於是范祖禹言：「京再執政，初與王安石不合，後為呂惠卿所傾，其中立不倚之操，為先帝稱挹。

translations.literal: Thereupon Fan Zuyu said, "Jing served twice in government; at first he did not agree with Wang Anshi, later was overthrown by Lü Huiqing—his upright, independent character was praised by the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zuyu then said, "Jing has held office twice: he first opposed Wang Anshi, then was brought down by Lü Huiqing, yet his impartial, unyielding conduct won the late emperor's esteem.

sentences.zh: 且昭陵學士，獨京一人存，若付以樞密，必允公論。」

translations.literal: Moreover, of the academicians from Zhaoling's reign, Jing alone survives; if entrusted with the Bureau of Military Affairs, public opinion would surely be satisfied."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, of the scholars who served under Emperor Zhenzong, Jing alone still lives; if he were placed in charge of military affairs, public opinion would surely approve."

sentences.zh: 時京已老，乃以為中太一宮使兼侍講，改宣徽南院使，拜太子少師，致仕。

translations.literal: By then Jing was already old; he was therefore made commissioner of the Central Grand Unity Palace and concurrent lecturer, transferred to commissioner of the Southern Court of the Palace Attendant Service, appointed Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and retired.
translations.idiomatic: By then Jing was already elderly; he was therefore made commissioner of the Central Grand Unity Palace with concurrent duties as lecturer, then commissioner of the Southern Court of the Palace Attendant Service, appointed Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 紹聖元年，薨，年七十四。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaosheng he died at age seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Shaosheng era he died at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 帝臨奠於第，贈司徒，諡曰文簡。

translations.literal: The emperor came in person to offer condolences at his residence; he was posthumously granted Grand Mentor and given the posthumous title Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came in person to mourn at his home; Jing was posthumously made Grand Mentor and given the posthumous title Wenjian ("Cultured and Simple").

sentences.zh: 始，京鄉居，受恩通判南宮成，迨貴，以郊恩官其子。

translations.literal: At the beginning, while living in his home village, Jing had received kindness from Cheng, the supervisory official of Nangong; when he rose to eminence, he used an imperial grace amnesty to grant Cheng's son an official post.
translations.idiomatic: In his early days at home, Jing had been obliged to Cheng, the supervisory official of Nangong; once he had risen high, he used an imperial amnesty to grant Cheng's son an official appointment.

sentences.zh: 嘗過外兄朱適，出侍妾，詢知為同年進士妻，亟請而嫁之。

translations.literal: Once when visiting his cousin Zhu Shi, Shi produced a concubine; upon inquiry Jing learned she was the wife of a fellow jinshi of the same year, and he urgently requested her and had her married off.
translations.idiomatic: On a visit to his cousin Zhu Shi, Shi presented a concubine; learning that she was the wife of a jinshi who had passed the examinations in the same year, Jing immediately asked for her release and saw that she was properly married.

sentences.zh: 其為郡守，諸縣公事至，即歷究之，苟與縣牘合而處斷麗於法者，呼法吏決罪，不以侍獄。

translations.literal: As a prefect, whenever county business arrived, he would exhaustively investigate it; if it matched the county documents and the judgment accorded with law, he summoned the legal clerk to pronounce sentence—he did not keep people awaiting trial in custody.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect, whenever county business reached him he examined it thoroughly; if the facts matched the county records and the ruling fit the law, he had the legal clerk pronounce sentence at once rather than holding people in jail.

sentences.zh: 報下捷疾，一無壅滯，人服其敏雲。

translations.literal: His reports went down swiftly, with not a single obstruction; people admired his efficiency.
translations.idiomatic: His decisions went out quickly, without a single backlog, and people admired his dispatch.

sentences.zh: 錢惟演

translations.literal: Qian Weiyan
translations.idiomatic: Qian Weiyan

sentences.zh: 錢惟演，字希聖，吳越王俶之子也，少補牙門將，從俶歸朝，為右屯衛將軍。

translations.literal: Qian Weiyan, courtesy name Xisheng, was a son of Qian Chu, king of Wuyue; in youth he was appointed gate guard general; following Chu in surrendering to the court, he was made General of the Right Garrison Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Weiyan, whose style name was Xisheng, was a son of Qian Chu, king of Wuyue; in youth he served as a gate guard general, and after Chu submitted to the Song he was made General of the Right Garrison Guard.

sentences.zh: 歷右神武軍將軍。

translations.literal: He served as General of the Right Divine Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General of the Right Divine Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 博學能文辭，召試學士院，以笏起草立就，真宗稱善。

translations.literal: Broadly learned and skilled in literary composition, he was summoned for examination at the Academy of Academicians; drafting with his tablet in hand, he finished at once—the True Emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned and gifted in letters, he was called to examination at the Hanlin Academy; holding his tablet, he finished a draft on the spot, and Emperor Zhenzong commended him.

sentences.zh: 改太僕少卿，獻《咸平聖政錄》。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of the Stud and presented the Records of Sacred Governance in the Xianping Era.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Minister of the Stud and submitted the Records of Sacred Governance in the Xianping Era.

sentences.zh: 命真秘閣，預修《《冊府元龜》，詔與楊億分為之序。

translations.literal: Appointed to the True Secret Archive, he participated in compiling the Prime Tortoise of the Book Archive; an edict had him and Yang Yi each write a preface.
translations.idiomatic: Assigned to the True Secret Archive, he took part in compiling the Prime Tortoise of the Book Archive, and an edict directed him and Yang Yi each to compose a preface.

sentences.zh: 除尚書司封郎中、知制誥，再遷給事中、知審官院。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Ministry of Personnel Office in the Ministry of Revenue, drafter of edicts; again promoted to Secretarial Recipient and director of the Bureau of Examining Officials.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Director of the Ministry of Personnel Office in the Ministry of Revenue and drafter of edicts, then promoted again to Secretarial Recipient and director of the Bureau of Examining Officials.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符八年，為翰林學士，坐私謁事罷之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, he became Hanlin academician; for the offense of a private visit he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he became Hanlin academician, but was removed for making an unauthorized private visit.

sentences.zh: 尋遷尚書工部侍郎，再為學土、會靈觀副使。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works, again made Hanlin academician and deputy commissioner of the Hall of Numinous Accord.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works and again made Hanlin academician and deputy commissioner of the Hall of Numinous Accord.

sentences.zh: 又坐貢舉失實，降給事中。

translations.literal: Again for the offense of untruth in the examination and recommendation process, he was demoted to Secretarial Recipient.
translations.idiomatic: He was again punished for misrepresenting the results of an examination and was demoted to Secretarial Recipient.

sentences.zh: 復工部侍郎，擢樞密副使、會靈觀使兼太子賓客，更領祥源觀。

translations.literal: Restored to Vice Minister of Works, promoted to vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, commissioner of the Hall of Numinous Accord and concurrent Host of the Heir Apparent, and further put in charge of the Hall of Auspicious Source.
translations.idiomatic: Restored to Vice Minister of Works, he was promoted to vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, made commissioner of the Hall of Numinous Accord and concurrent Host of the Heir Apparent, and given charge of the Hall of Auspicious Source as well.

sentences.zh: 累遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was progressively promoted to Minister of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted step by step to Minister of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，進兵部。

translations.literal: When Renzong acceded, he was advanced to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong came to the throne, he was promoted to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 王曾為相，以惟演嘗位曾上，因拜樞密使。

translations.literal: When Wang Zeng became chief councilor, because Weiyan had once ranked above Zeng, he was appointed commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zeng became chief councilor, Weiyan was made commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs because he had once outranked Zeng.

sentences.zh: 故事，樞密使必加檢校官，惟演止以尚書充使，有司之失也。

translations.literal: By precedent, the military affairs commissioner must receive an honorary inspection title; Weiyan served solely as minister—an oversight of the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: By custom a military affairs commissioner was always given an honorary inspection title, but Weiyan served with only his ministerial rank—a lapse on the part of the responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 初，惟演見丁謂權盛，附之，與為婚。

translations.literal: At first, seeing Ding Wei's power flourishing, Weiyan attached himself to him and entered into marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: At first, seeing Ding Wei's ascendancy, Weiyan attached himself to him and formed a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 謂逐寇準，惟演與有力焉。

translations.literal: When Ding drove out Kou Zhun, Weiyan had a hand in it.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding forced Kou Zhun from office, Weiyan helped bring it about.

sentences.zh: 及序樞密題名，獨刊去準，名曰「逆準」，削而不書。

translations.literal: When listing names at the Bureau of Military Affairs, he alone excised Zhun, calling him "Rebel Zhun"—cut out and not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: When the Bureau compiled its roster of names, he alone struck out Zhun, labeling him "Rebel Zhun" and omitting him from the record.

sentences.zh: 謂禍既萌，惟演慮並得罪，遂擠謂以自解。

translations.literal: Once Ding's disaster had sprouted, Weiyan feared being implicated and so pushed Ding aside to exonerate himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding's downfall began, Weiyan, fearing he would be implicated, turned on Ding to clear himself.

sentences.zh: 宰相馮拯惡其為人，因言：「惟演以妹妻劉美，乃太后姻家，不可與機政，請出之。」

translations.literal: Chief councilor Feng Zheng detested his character and said, "Weiyan gave his sister in marriage to Liu Mei—part of the empress dowager's affinal family—he must not share in state secrets; please send him out."
translations.idiomatic: Chief councilor Feng Zheng, disliking his conduct, said, "Weiyan married his sister to Liu Mei, a kinsman of the empress dowager; he must not hold military secrets—please remove him from court."

sentences.zh: 乃罷為鎮國軍節度觀察留後，即日改保大軍節度使、知河陽。

translations.literal: He was dismissed to be military observation commissioner-at-large of Zhenguo Army, and the same day transferred to military commissioner of Baoda Army and prefect of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed to serve as military observation commissioner-at-large of the Zhenguo Army, and that same day was transferred to military commissioner of the Baoda Army and prefect of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 逾年，請入朝，加同中書門下平章事、判許州。

translations.literal: After a year he requested to enter court; he was given the title of Grand Councilor Concurrently Minister of Affairs and assigned to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he asked to return to court and was given the title of Grand Councilor Concurrently Minister of Affairs with assignment to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 未即行，冀復用，侍御史鞠詠奏劾之，惟演乃亟去。

translations.literal: Without departing immediately, hoping to be reused, Remonstrating Censor Ju Yong memorialized to impeach him, and Weiyan then hurried away.
translations.idiomatic: He did not leave at once, hoping to be recalled; Remonstrating Censor Ju Yong impeached him, and Weiyan then departed in haste.

sentences.zh: 天聖七年，改武勝軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tiansheng, he was transferred to military commissioner of Wusheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tiansheng he was transferred to military commissioner of the Wusheng Army.

sentences.zh: 明年來朝，上言先壠在洛陽，願守宮鑰。

translations.literal: The next year he came to court and stated that his ancestral tombs were at Luoyang; he wished to guard the palace keys.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he came to court and said his ancestral graves lay at Luoyang; he asked to hold the keys to the palace there.

sentences.zh: 即以判河南府，再改泰寧軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was immediately made prefect of Henan prefecture, then again transferred to military commissioner of Taining Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was at once appointed prefect of Henan and later transferred again to military commissioner of the Taining Army.

sentences.zh: 惟演雅意柄用，抑鬱不得志。

translations.literal: Weiyan had always aspired to wield power; depressed and frustrated in his ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyan had long coveted real power and was now depressed and thwarted in his ambitions.

sentences.zh: 及帝耕籍田，求侍祠，因留為景靈宮使。

translations.literal: When the emperor plowed the sacred field, he sought to attend the rites and was retained as commissioner of the Hall of Splendid Numen.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor performed the plowing rite, Weiyan asked to assist in the ceremony and was kept on as commissioner of the Hall of Splendid Numen.

sentences.zh: 太后崩，詔還河南。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager died, an edict ordered him back to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: After the empress dowager died, an edict sent him back to Henan.

sentences.zh: 惟演不自安，請以庄獻明肅太后、庄懿太后並配真宗廟室，以希帝意。

translations.literal: Weiyan felt insecure; he requested that Empress Dowager Zhuangxian Mingsu and Empress Dowager Zhuangyi both be enshrined in Emperor Zhenzong's temple to court the emperor's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy in his position, Weiyan proposed that Empresses Dowager Zhuangxian Mingsu and Zhuangyi both be enshrined in Emperor Zhenzong's temple, hoping to win the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 惟演既與劉美親，又為其子曖娶郭后妹，至是，又欲與庄懿太后族為婚。

translations.literal: Weiyan had already been kin to Liu Mei and had his son Ai marry Empress Guo's sister; at this point he again sought marriage alliance with Empress Dowager Zhuangyi's clan.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyan was already related to Liu Mei and had his son Ai marry a sister of Empress Guo; now he sought yet another marriage tie with the clan of Empress Dowager Zhuangyi.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞范諷劾惟演擅議宗廟，且與後家通婚姻。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Fan Feng impeached Weiyan for presumptuously debating the ancestral temple and intermarrying with the empress's family.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Fan Feng impeached Weiyan for meddling in ancestral temple matters and forming marriage ties with the empress's kin.

sentences.zh: 落平章事，為崇信軍節度使，歸本鎮。

translations.literal: Stripped of grand councilor status, he was made military commissioner of Chongxin Army and returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of his grand councilor title, he was made military commissioner of the Chongxin Army and sent back to his former post.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，特贈侍中。

translations.literal: Before long he died; specially granted Palace Attendant posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward and was specially granted the posthumous rank of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 太常張瑰按，《諡法》敏而好學曰「文」，貪而敗官曰「墨」，請諡文墨。

translations.literal: Director of Ritual Zhang Gui consulted the Treatise on Posthumous Names—"keen and fond of learning" is Wen, "greedy and ruining office" is Mo—and requested the posthumous name Wenmo.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Ritual Zhang Gui, citing the Treatise on Posthumous Names—where "keen and fond of learning" yields Wen and "greedy and ruining office" yields Mo—proposed the posthumous name Wenmo.

sentences.zh: 其家訴於朝，詔章得象等覆議，以惟演無貪黷狀，而晚節率職自新，有惶懼可憐之意，取《諡法》追悔前過曰「思」，改諡曰思。

translations.literal: His family appealed to court; an edict had Zhang Dexiang and others review it—finding no evidence of Weiyan's greed and corruption, and that in his later years he fulfilled duties and reformed, with a pitiable sense of apprehension—they took from the Treatise on Posthumous Names "regretting past faults" as Si, and changed the posthumous name to Si.
translations.idiomatic: His family appealed to the throne; an edict ordered Zhang Dexiang and others to reconsider the case. Finding no proof of corruption and noting that in his later years Weiyan had served conscientiously and shown remorse, they applied the Treatise on Posthumous Names' criterion "regretting past faults" and changed the posthumous name to Si.

sentences.zh: 慶歷間，二太后始升祔真宗廟室，子曖復訴前議，乃改諡曰文僖。

translations.literal: During Qingli, the two empresses dowagers were first elevated to enshrinement in Zhenzong's temple; son Ai again appealed the earlier decision, and the posthumous name was changed to Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingli era, when the two empresses dowagers were first enshrined in Zhenzong's temple, his son Ai renewed the family's appeal, and the posthumous name was changed to Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 惟演出於勛貴，文辭清麗，名與楊億、劉筠相上下。

translations.literal: Weiyan came from meritorious nobility; his literary style was elegant, his reputation on par with Yang Yi and Liu Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Born into a house of merit, Weiyan wrote in a refined style and stood in reputation alongside Yang Yi and Liu Yun.

sentences.zh: 於書無所不讀，家儲文籍侔秘府。

translations.literal: He read everything; his home's stored books rivaled the secret archive.
translations.idiomatic: There was scarcely a book he had not read, and the library in his home rivaled the imperial archive.

sentences.zh: 尤喜獎厲後進。

translations.literal: He especially delighted in encouraging rising talent.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially fond of encouraging younger scholars.

sentences.zh: 初，真宗諡號稱「文」，惟演曰「真宗幸澶淵御契丹，盟而服之，宜兼諡『武』。

translations.literal: At first, Emperor Zhenzong's posthumous title included Wen; Weiyan said, "Emperor Zhenzong went to Chanyuan to face the Khitan, made a covenant and subdued them—he should also receive the posthumous element Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong's posthumous title was first proposed as Wen, Weiyan argued, "The emperor went to Chanyuan to confront the Khitan, made peace, and brought them to submission; he should also bear the element Wu.

sentences.zh: 下有司議，乃加諡「武定」。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the responsible offices for discussion, and Wuding was added.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was referred to the responsible offices, and the additional element Wuding ("Martial and Settled") was approved.

sentences.zh: 所著《典懿集》三十卷，又著《金坡遺事》、《飛白書敘錄》《逢辰錄》、《奉藩書事》。

translations.literal: He authored thirty juan of the Collection of Canonical Elegance and also wrote Remnants from the Golden Slope, Record of Flying-White Calligraphy, Record of Fortunate Days, and Affairs of Serving the Fief.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote thirty juan of the Collection of Canonical Elegance, as well as Remnants from the Golden Slope, Record of Flying-White Calligraphy, Record of Fortunate Days, and Affairs of Serving the Fief.

sentences.zh: 惟演嘗語人曰：「吾平生不足者，惟不得於黃紙上押字爾。」

translations.literal: Weiyan once told people, "In my life the one thing lacking is only that I never got to sign my name on yellow paper."
translations.idiomatic: Weiyan once said to others, "The one thing I have lacked in life is the chance to affix my signature to yellow paper."

sentences.zh: 蓋未嘗歷中書故也。

translations.literal: This was because he had never served in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He meant that he had never held office in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子曖、晦、暄，從弟易。

translations.literal: His sons were Ai, Hui, and Xuan; his cousin was Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Ai, Hui, and Xuan; his younger cousin was Yi.

sentences.zh: 晦字明叔，以大理評事娶獻穆大長公主女，累遷東上閣門使、貴州團練使。

translations.literal: Hui, courtesy name Mingshu, as an auditor of the Court of Judicial Review married the daughter of the Grand Eldest Princess Xianmu; he was successively promoted to Eastern Upper Gate envoy and regimental commander of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hui, styled Mingshu, married the daughter of the Grand Eldest Princess Xianmu while serving as an auditor of the Court of Judicial Review; he rose to Eastern Upper Gate envoy and regimental commander of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 王守忠領兩使留後，移閣門定朝立燕坐位，晦因言：「天子大朝會，令宦者齒士大夫坐殿上，必為外夷所笑。」

translations.literal: Wang Shouzhong held the two commissioner-at-large posts; he moved the Gate office to set seating for court assemblies and banquet standing positions; Hui then said, "At the emperor's great court assembly, to have eunuchs sit on equal footing with scholar-officials in the hall will surely be mocked by foreign barbarians."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shouzhong, holding two commissioner-at-large posts, had the Gate office rearrange seating for court sessions and banquet protocol; Hui objected, "At the emperor's great assembly, to seat eunuchs alongside scholar-officials in the hall will surely be laughed at by foreign envoys."

sentences.zh: 守忠更欲以禮服進酒，晦又以為不可。

translations.literal: Shouzhong further wished to have them advance wine in ceremonial dress; Hui again considered this unacceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhong also wanted eunuchs to present wine in full ceremonial dress, which Hui again rejected.

sentences.zh: 勾當三班院、群牧都監，授忠州防禦使、知河中府。

translations.literal: He served as acting director of the Three-Class Academy and chief overseer of the Pasture Office; he was granted Defender of Zhongzhou and made prefect of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting director of the Three-Class Academy and chief overseer of the Pasture Office, then was granted the rank of Defender of Zhongzhou and appointed prefect of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 帝因戒曰：「陝西方罷兵，民困久矣。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon admonished him, "Shaanxi has only just ceased warfare; the people have long been impoverished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then warned him, "Shaanxi has only just seen fighting end; the people there have long been exhausted.

sentences.zh: 卿為朕愛撫，毋縱酒樂，使人呼為貴戚子弟也。」

translations.literal: Serve me by cherishing and soothing them; do not indulge in wine and music, lest people call you a pampered imperial relative."
translations.idiomatic: Care for them on my behalf; do not give yourself over to wine and music, or people will dismiss you as a spoiled imperial in-law."

sentences.zh: 晦頓首謝。

translations.literal: Hui bowed his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Hui kowtowed in acknowledgment.

sentences.zh: 改潁州防禦使，為秦鳳路馬步軍總管。

translations.literal: Transferred to Defender of Yingzhou, he became overall commander of cavalry and infantry of Qinfeng Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Defender of Yingzhou, he was made overall commander of cavalry and infantry on the Qinfeng Circuit.

sentences.zh: 復還三班院，同提舉集禧觀。

translations.literal: He returned to the Three-Class Academy and concurrently supervised the Hall of Gathered Blessings.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the Three-Class Academy and concurrently supervised the Hall of Gathered Blessings.

sentences.zh: 歷霸州防禦使，為群牧副使，卒。

translations.literal: He served as Defender of Bazhou, became deputy overseer of the Pasture Office, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Defender of Bazhou, then as deputy overseer of the Pasture Office, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 暄字載陽，以父蔭累官駕部郎中、知撫州，移台州。

translations.literal: Xuan, courtesy name Zaiyang, through his father's privilege rose to Director of the Ministry of Ceremonials and prefect of Fuzhou, then transferred to Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, styled Zaiyang, entered office through his father's privilege and rose to Director of the Ministry of Ceremonials and prefect of Fuzhou before being transferred to Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 台城惡地下，秋潦暴集，輒圮溺，人多即山為居。

translations.literal: Taizhou's walls stood on poor ground; autumn floods would suddenly gather, and they repeatedly collapsed and flooded; many people built dwellings on the hills.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhou stood on low, unstable ground; autumn floods would rush in and repeatedly breach the walls, so many residents built homes on the hills.

sentences.zh: 暄為增治城堞，壘石為台，作大堤捍之。

translations.literal: Xuan had the battlements repaired and strengthened, piled stone to build platforms, and constructed a great dike to hold back the water.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan strengthened the battlements, piled stone into platforms, and built a great embankment to hold back the floods.

sentences.zh: 進少府監、權鹽鐵副使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Palace Manufactories and acting vice commissioner of Salt and Iron.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Palace Manufactories and acting vice commissioner of the Salt and Iron Commission.

sentences.zh: 暄鉤考諸路逋租，兩浙轉運使負課當坐，暄上言：「浙部仍歲飢，故租賦不登籍，今使者獲罪，必亟斂於民，民不堪矣。」

translations.literal: Xuan audited delinquent rent across circuits; the transport commissioner of the Two Zhe had failed to meet tax quotas and should be punished; Xuan memorialized, "The Zhe region has suffered famine year after year, so rent and tax could not be entered in the registers; if the commissioner is now punished, taxes will surely be squeezed from the people at once—the people cannot bear it."
translations.idiomatic: While auditing delinquent rents on the circuits, Xuan found that the transport commissioner of the Two Zhe districts had failed to meet his quota and faced punishment; he memorialized, "The Zhe region has suffered famine year after year, so taxes could not be fully recorded; if this official is punished now, the shortfall will be wrung from the people at once, and they cannot endure it."

sentences.zh: 神宗即詔釋之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong immediately issued an edict releasing him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong immediately issued an edict pardoning the commissioner.

sentences.zh: 官制行，為光祿卿，出知鄆州，拜寶文閣待制，卒。

translations.literal: When the new office system took effect, he became Director of the Imperial Household Food and went out as prefect of Yanzhou; he was granted awaiting draft in the Hall of Treasured Culture and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the new bureaucratic system was implemented, he became Director of the Imperial Household Food, then went out as prefect of Yanzhou; he was granted awaiting draft in the Hall of Treasured Culture and died.

sentences.zh: 子景臻，尚秦、魯國大長公主。

translations.literal: His son Jingzhen married the Grand Eldest Princess of the States of Qin and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingzhen married the Grand Eldest Princess of the States of Qin and Lu.

sentences.zh: 景臻子忱，在《外戚傳》。

translations.literal: Jingzhen's son Chen is treated in the Biographies of the Empresses' Kin.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhen's son Chen is treated in the Biographies of the Empresses' Kin.

sentences.zh: 從弟 易

translations.literal: Younger cousin Yi
translations.idiomatic: Younger cousin Yi

sentences.zh: 易字希白。

translations.literal: Yi styled himself Xibai.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, styled Xibai.

sentences.zh: 始，父倧嗣吳越王，為大將胡進思所廢，而立其弟俶。

translations.literal: At the beginning, his father Zong succeeded to the kingship of Wuyue, was deposed by the great general Hu Jinsi, and his younger brother Chu was enthroned in his place.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning, his father Zong had inherited the throne of the King of Wuyue but was deposed by the great general Hu Jinsi, who enthroned his younger brother Chu instead.

sentences.zh: 俶歸朝，群從悉補官，易與兄昆不見錄，遂刻志讀書。

translations.literal: When Chu submitted to the court, all the collateral kin were given official appointments, but Yi and his elder brother Kun were not recorded for advancement, so they resolved their will to study books.
translations.idiomatic: After Chu surrendered to the Song court, all the collateral branch of the family received official appointments, but Yi and his elder brother Kun were passed over; they therefore devoted themselves wholeheartedly to study.

sentences.zh: 昆字裕之，舉進士，為治寬簡便民，能詩，善草隸書，累官右諫議大夫，以秘書監於家。

translations.literal: Kun styled himself Yuzhi, passed the jinshi examination, in governance was lenient and simple and benefited the people, could compose poetry, was skilled at cursive and clerical script, rose through offices to Right Remonstrance Censor, and ended his career as Supervisor of the Palace Library at home.
translations.idiomatic: Kun, styled Yuzhi, passed the jinshi examination. His administration was lenient and unpretentious and brought convenience to the people. He could write poetry and excelled at cursive and clerical calligraphy. He rose through office to Right Remonstrance Censor and retired at home as Supervisor of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 易年十七，舉進士，試崇政殿，三篇，日未中而就。

translations.literal: When Yi was seventeen he passed the jinshi examination, was tested in the Chongzheng Hall with three compositions, and finished before the sun reached midday.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen, Yi passed the jinshi examination. Tested in the Chongzheng Hall on three compositions, he finished before noon.

sentences.zh: 言者惡其輕俊，特罷之。

translations.literal: Those who spoke at court disliked his light cleverness and specially disqualified him.
translations.idiomatic: Critics at court resented his precocious flippancy and had him disqualified.

sentences.zh: 然自此以才藻知名。

translations.literal: Nevertheless, from this time he became renowned for literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, from that point on he was known for his literary brilliance.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗與蘇易簡論唐世文人，嘆時無李白。

translations.literal: Taizong once discussed Tang-dynasty literati with Su Yijian and sighed that the age had no Li Bai.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong once discussed Tang literary figures with Su Yijian and lamented that the age produced no one like Li Bai.

sentences.zh: 易簡曰：「今進士錢易，為歌詩殆不下白。」

translations.literal: Yijian said: "Present jinshi Qian Yi, in composing song-poetry, is almost not inferior to Bai."
translations.idiomatic: Su Yijian replied, "The current jinshi Qian Yi writes lyrics that rival Li Bai's nearly as well."

sentences.zh: 太宗驚喜曰：「誠然，吾當自布衣召置翰林。」

translations.literal: Taizong, startled and pleased, said: "It is truly so; I shall summon him from commoner status and appoint him to the Hanlin."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was startled and delighted. "That is true," he said. "I shall summon him straight from common life and place him in the Hanlin Academy."

sentences.zh: 值盜起劍南，遂寢。

translations.literal: Just then bandits rose in Jiannan, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: But banditry broke out in Jiannan just then, and the plan was shelved.

sentences.zh: 真宗在東宮，圖山水扇，會易作歌，賞愛之。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong was in the Eastern Palace, he painted a landscape on a fan; as it happened Yi composed a song for it, and he admired and loved it.
translations.idiomatic: While still heir apparent, Zhenzong painted a landscape fan; Yi happened to write a lyric for it, which the future emperor greatly admired.

sentences.zh: 易再舉進士，就開封府試第二。

translations.literal: Yi again competed for the jinshi degree and placed second on the Kaifeng prefectural examination.
translations.idiomatic: Yi tried again for the jinshi degree and finished second on the Kaifeng prefectural examination.

sentences.zh: 自謂當第一，為有司所屈，乃上書言試《朽索之馭六馬賦》，意涉譏諷。

translations.literal: He considered that he should have ranked first and had been wronged by the authorities; he therefore submitted a memorial stating that in the examination fu on "Driving Six Horses with a Rotten Rope," his intent touched on satire.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced he deserved first place and had been unfairly held down by the examiners, he submitted a memorial about his fu titled "Driving Six Horses with a Rotten Rope," arguing that its meaning had been read as satirical.

sentences.zh: 真宗惡其無行，降第二。

translations.literal: Zhenzong hated his unseemly conduct and demoted him to second rank.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong took offense at his improper behavior and had him reduced to second place.

sentences.zh: 明年，第二人中第，補濠州團練推官。

translations.literal: The following year, as second-ranked graduate he passed the degree and was appointed as pushan on the Hao Prefecture circuit-training staff.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he passed as second-ranked graduate and was appointed military pushan on the Hao prefectural staff.

sentences.zh: 召試中書，改光祿寺丞、通判蘄州。

translations.literal: Summoned to examination at the Central Secretariat, he was transferred to Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and concurrently served as administrative prefect of Qiz Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Called to a special examination at the Secretariat, he was made Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and assigned as administrative prefect of Qiz Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 奏疏曰：「堯放四罪而不言殺，彼四者之凶，尚惡言殺，非堯仁之至乎？

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: "Yao banished the four criminals without speaking of killing; those four were wicked, yet even they hated to speak of killing—is this not the utmost of Yao's benevolence?
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "Yao banished the Four Criminals without a word about execution. Men so wicked as they still shrank from speaking of killing—is that not the supreme expression of Yao's humanity?

sentences.zh: 古之肉刑者劓、椓、黥、刖皆非死，尚以為虐。

translations.literal: The corporal punishments of antiquity—nose-cutting, ear-cutting, tattooing, and foot-cutting—were none of them death, yet they were still regarded as cruel.
translations.idiomatic: The bodily punishments of antiquity—nose cutting, ear mutilation, tattooing, and amputation of the feet—none of them entailed death, yet even these were considered barbarous.

sentences.zh: 近代以來，斷人手足，鉤背烙筋，身見白骨而猶視息，四體分落乃方絕命。

translations.literal: From recent times forward, men's hands and feet have been severed, backs hooked and sinews branded, while the body still shows white bone and yet draws breath; only when the four limbs are severed does life finally end.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times offenders have had their limbs severed, their backs hooked and their sinews branded with hot irons, left alive until the bone shows white and breath still comes—death arriving only after the body has been torn limb from limb.

sentences.zh: 以此示人，非平世事也。

translations.literal: To display this to people is not the business of a peaceful age.
translations.idiomatic: To parade such punishments before the public is unworthy of an age of peace.

sentences.zh: 今四方長吏競為殘暴，婺州先斷賊手足，然後斬之以聞。

translations.literal: Now throughout the realm chief officials compete in cruelty; in Wu Prefecture thieves' hands and feet are first cut off, and only then they are beheaded and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Today local magistrates everywhere vie in cruelty. In Wu Prefecture thieves first have their limbs cut off and are then beheaded before the fact is reported to court.

sentences.zh: 壽州巡檢使磔賊於闤闠之中，其旁猶有盜物者。

translations.literal: The circuit inspector of Shou Prefecture dismembered thieves in the marketplace, while beside them people were still stealing goods.
translations.idiomatic: The Shou Prefecture circuit inspector had thieves publicly dismembered in the market square—while looters still plundered goods beside the scaffold.

sentences.zh: 使嚴刑可誡於眾，則秦之天下無叛民矣。

translations.literal: If harsh punishments could truly warn the multitude, then in Qin's realm there would have been no rebellious people.
translations.idiomatic: If harsh punishment alone could deter the masses, the Qin empire would never have known rebellion.

sentences.zh: 臣以謂非法之刑，非所以助治，惟陛下除之。」

translations.literal: Your subject considers that punishments outside the law do not aid governance; Your Majesty alone should abolish them."
translations.idiomatic: I submit that extra-legal punishments do not assist good governance. Your Majesty alone can abolish them."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納其言。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the memorial and adopted his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 景德中，舉賢良方正科，策入等，除秘書丞、通判信州。

translations.literal: During the Jingde era he was nominated for the category of worthies of upright character; his policy essay entered the ranks, and he was appointed as Secretary of the Palace Library and administrative prefect of Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingde reign he entered the "worthies and upright scholars" examination; his policy essay qualified and he was appointed Secretary of the Palace Library and administrative prefect of Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 東封泰山，獻《殊祥錄》，改太常博士、直集賢院。

translations.literal: When the emperor performed the eastern feng at Mount Tai, he presented "Record of Exceptional Omens" and was transferred to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and appointed as a direct academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: When the court conducted the eastern feng sacrifice at Mount Tai, he submitted "Record of Exceptional Omens" and was made Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and a direct academician in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 祀汾陰，幸亳州，命修《車駕所過圖經》，獻《宋雅》一篇，遷尚書祠部員外郎。

translations.literal: When the emperor sacrificed at Fenyin and visited Boz Prefecture, he was ordered to compile "Gazetteers of Places the Imperial Carriage Passed," presented one piece of "Song Elegantiae," and was promoted to Assistant Director of the Ministry of Rites' Sacrifice office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Fenyin sacrifice and the imperial visit to Boz, he was charged with compiling the "Gazetteers of Places the Imperial Procession Traversed," submitted a piece for "Song Elegantiae," and was promoted to Assistant Director in the Sacrifices Office of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 坐發國子監諸科非其人，降監潁州稅。

translations.literal: Because he had recommended unworthy men for various categories in the Directorate of Education, he was demoted to tax supervisor at Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Ying Prefecture grain-tax supervisor for having advanced unsuitable candidates in various categories at the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 數月，召還。

translations.literal: After several months he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 久之，判三司磨勘司。

translations.literal: After some time he was assigned to adjudicate the Three Departments review office.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he was put in charge of the Three Departments review office.

sentences.zh: 上言：「官物在籍，而三司移文釐正，或其數細微，輒歷年不得報，徒擾州縣。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial: "Official goods are on the registers, yet when the Three Departments dispatch documents to correct discrepancies, even if the amounts are minute, years may pass without reply, merely troubling prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "When registered government goods are scrutinized, the Three Departments dispatch correction orders even for the smallest discrepancies—then years pass with no resolution, needlessly harassing local governments.

sentences.zh: 自今官錢百、谷斗、帛二尺以下，非欺紿者除之。」

translations.literal: From now on, for official coin of one hundred or less, grain of one dou or less, and silk of two chi or less, unless fraud is involved, eliminate the cases."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth discrepancies under one hundred cash, one dou of grain, or two chi of silk should be waived unless deliberate fraud is involved."

sentences.zh: 真宗雅眷詞臣，其典掌誥命，皆躬自柬拔。

translations.literal: Zhenzong greatly favored literary officials; those charged with drafting proclamations and edicts he personally selected.
