translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong especially favored literary officials; every appointment to draft edicts and proclamations he made in person.

sentences.zh: 擢知制誥、判登聞鼓院、糾察在京刑獄。

translations.literal: He was elevated to Drafting Proclamations, assigned to judge the Petition Drum Court, and to investigate capital criminal cases in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Drafting Proclamations, assigned to the Petition Drum Court, and charged with inspecting capital criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 累遷左司郎中，為翰林學士，

translations.literal: After successive promotions he became Left Department Director and was made Hanlin Academician,
translations.idiomatic: After successive promotions he reached Left Department Director and was appointed Hanlin Academician,

sentences.zh: 儤直未滿，卒。

translations.literal: before his turn of duty watch was complete, he died.
translations.idiomatic: but died before completing his rotation of duty at court.

sentences.zh: 仁宗憐之，召其妻盛氏至禁中，賜以冠帔。

translations.literal: Renzong pitied him, summoned his wife Lady Sheng into the inner palace, and bestowed on her cap and sash of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong took pity on him and summoned his wife, Lady Sheng, into the palace, granting her official cap and robes.

sentences.zh: 易才學瞻敏過人，數千百言，援筆立就。

translations.literal: Yi in talent and learning was perceptive and quick beyond others; compositions of several thousand or several hundred words he completed the moment his brush touched paper.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's talent and learning surpassed ordinary men: essays of hundreds or thousands of words flowed from his brush as soon as he picked up the pen.

sentences.zh: 又善尋尺大書行草，及喜觀佛書，嘗校《道藏經》，著《殺生戒》，有《金閨》、《瀛州》、《西垣制集》一百五十卷，《青雲總錄》、《青雲新錄》《南部新書》、《洞微志》一百三十卷。

translations.literal: Further, he was skilled at large cursive and running script measured in chi and cun, and enjoyed reading Buddhist books; he once collated the Daoist Canon, authored "Admonition against Killing," and had "Golden Inner Chambers," "Prefecture of Ying," and "Collected Drafts from the Western Enclosure" in one hundred fifty volumes, and "General Record of Azure Clouds," "New Record of Azure Clouds," "New Book of the Southern Department," and "Record of Subtle Penetration" in one hundred thirty volumes.
translations.idiomatic: He also excelled at large-scale running and cursive calligraphy, delighted in reading Buddhist texts, once collated the Daoist Canon, and wrote "Admonition against Killing." His published works included "Golden Inner Chambers," "Prefecture of Ying," and "Collected Drafts from the Western Enclosure" in one hundred fifty volumes, and "General Record of Azure Clouds," "New Record of Azure Clouds," "New Book of the Southern Department," and "Record of Subtle Penetration" in one hundred thirty volumes.

sentences.zh: 子彥遠、明逸，相繼皆以賢良方正應詔。

translations.literal: His sons Yanyuan and Mingyi successively both responded to imperial summons in the worthies and upright category.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Yanyuan and Mingyi both answered successive imperial summons in the "worthies and upright scholars" category.

sentences.zh: 宋興以來，父子兄弟制策登科者，錢氏一家而已。

translations.literal: Since the rise of Song, of fathers and sons and brothers who passed the policy-examination degree, only the Qian clan alone.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of the Song, the Qian family alone could claim fathers, sons, and brothers who had all passed the policy-examination degree.

sentences.zh: 易子 彥遠

translations.literal: Yi's son Yanyuan
translations.idiomatic: Yi's son Yanyuan

sentences.zh: 彥遠字子高，以父蔭補太廟齋郎，累遷大理寺丞。

translations.literal: Yanyuan styled himself Zigao, entered office by his father's yin privilege as Grand Temple Fast Officer, and through successive promotions became Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyuan, styled Zigao, entered service through his father's privilege as a Grand Temple Fast Officer and rose to Assistant Director in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 舉進士第，以殿中丞為御史台推直官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi degree and served as investigative officer of the Censorate as Palace Aide.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination he served the Censorate as investigative officer with the rank of Palace Aide.

sentences.zh: 通判明州，遷太常博士。

translations.literal: As administrative prefect of Ming Prefecture he was transferred to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He served as administrative prefect of Ming Prefecture and was then made Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 舉賢良方正能直言極諫科，擢尚書祠部員外郎、知潤州。

translations.literal: Nominated in the category of worthies of upright character able to speak frankly and remonstrate to the utmost, he was promoted to Assistant Director of the Ministry of Rites' Sacrifice office and appointed prefect of Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the "worthies and upright scholars who speak frankly and remonstrate to the utmost" category, he was promoted to Assistant Director in the Sacrifices Office and appointed prefect of Run Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 上疏曰：

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 陛下即位以來，內無聲色之娛，外無畋漁之樂，而前歲地震，雄、霸、滄、登，旁及荊湖，幅員數千里，雖往昔定襄之異，未甚於此。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, within there has been no pleasure in sound and color, without no delight in hunting and fishing; yet in the year before last earthquakes struck Xiong, Ba, Cang, and Deng, extending to Jing and Hu, covering several thousand li—though the anomaly of Dingxiang in the past was not so severe as this.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty's accession you have shunned sensual indulgence within the palace and hunting and fishing abroad, yet in the year before last earthquakes struck Xiong, Ba, Cang, and Deng and reached as far as Jing and Hu—thousands of li of territory—surpassing even the notorious Dingxiang omen of old.

sentences.zh: 今復大旱，人心嗷嗷，天其或者以陛下備寇之術未至，牧民之吏未良，天下之民未安，故出譴告以示之。

translations.literal: Now drought again is severe, and popular hearts cry out; Heaven perhaps means that Your Majesty's methods for preparing against enemies are not yet complete, the officials who shepherd the people are not yet good, and the people of the realm are not yet secure—therefore issuing reprimand and warning to show this.
translations.idiomatic: Now a great drought has come again and the people groan with distress. Perhaps Heaven means to warn that our defenses against enemies remain inadequate, that local magistrates are deficient, and that the realm is not yet at ease.

sentences.zh: 苟能順天之戒，增修德業，宗社之福也。

translations.literal: If we can follow Heaven's warning, increase and cultivate virtue and achievement, it will be the fortune of the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty heeds Heaven's warning and deepens your moral cultivation, the dynasty will be blessed.

sentences.zh: 今契丹據山後諸鎮，元昊盜靈武、銀、夏，衣冠車服，子女玉帛，莫不有之。

translations.literal: Now the Khitan hold the various posts beyond the mountains; Yuanhao has seized Lingwu, Yin, and Xia—robes and caps, carriages and regalia, children and jade silks, none is lacking.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan hold the frontier posts north of the mountains; Li Yuanhao has seized Lingwu, Yin, and Xia, enjoying robes and regalia, carriages and seals, retainers and tribute as if he were a true sovereign.

sentences.zh: 往時，元昊內寇，出入五載，天下騷然。

translations.literal: In former times Yuanhao raided within the borders, coming and going for five years, and the realm was in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao invaded earlier, war swept back and forth for five years and the empire was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 及納款賜命，則被邊長吏，不復銓擇，高冠大裾，恥言軍旅，一日契丹負恩，乘利入塞，豈特元昊之比耶？

translations.literal: When he submitted allegiance and received appointment, then the chief officials on the frontier were no longer examined and selected; wearing high caps and long robes, they were ashamed to speak of military affairs—if one day the Khitan prove ungrateful and seize advantage to enter the passes, will it be only Yuanhao's measure?
translations.idiomatic: After he submitted and received imperial investiture, frontier governors were no longer carefully chosen—men in high caps and flowing robes who disdained even to speak of warfare. If the Khitan should one day break faith and surge through the passes, would the danger be any less than Yuanhao's?

sentences.zh: 湖、廣蠻獠劫掠生民，調發督斂，軍須百出，三年於今，未聞分寸之效。

translations.literal: In Hu and Guang the Man and Liao bandits plunder the people; levies are dispatched and collections supervised, military supplies issue forth in every direction—for three years to this day, not a fraction of effect has been heard.
translations.idiomatic: In Hunan and Guangdong tribal peoples raid and plunder; requisitions and levies pour out in every direction—yet after three years there is no sign of success.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下念此三方之急，講長久之計，以上答天戒。

translations.literal: Only Your Majesty should consider the urgency of these three directions, devise a long-term plan, thereby to answer Heaven's warning above.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to address the crises on these three fronts and devise a lasting strategy to answer Heaven's warning.

sentences.zh: 時旱蝗，民乏食，彥遠發常平倉賑救之。

translations.literal: At the time of drought and locusts the people lacked food; Yanyuan opened the Ever-Normal Granary to relieve and save them.
translations.idiomatic: During drought and locust plague, when the people faced famine, Yanyuan opened the Ever-Normal Granary for relief.

sentences.zh: 部使者詰其專且搉價，彥遠不為屈。

translations.literal: The circuit commissioner questioned his unauthorized action and fixed pricing; Yanyuan did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit commissioner challenged his unauthorized distribution and price-setting, but Yanyuan stood firm.

sentences.zh: 召為右司諫，請勿數赦，擇牧守，增奉入以養廉吏，息土木以省功費。

translations.literal: Summoned as Right Secretariat Remonstrance Official, he requested that amnesties not be frequent, that prefects and governors be selected carefully, that salary income be increased to support upright officials, and that construction in earth and wood be stopped to save labor costs.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Right Secretariat Remonstrance Official, he urged less frequent amnesties, careful selection of prefects and governors, higher salaries to sustain honest officials, and a halt to construction projects to conserve the treasury.

sentences.zh: 遷起居舍人、直集賢院、知諫院。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Diarist, direct academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and head of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Diarist, made a direct academician in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and appointed head of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 會諸路奏大水，彥遠言陰氣過盛，在《五行傳》「下有謀上之象」，請嚴宮省宿衛。

translations.literal: Just then all circuits reported great floods; Yanyuan said yin force was excessive, that in "Treatise on the Five Phases" there is the image of "those below plotting against those above," and requested strict palace and secretariat guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: When every circuit reported catastrophic floods, Yanyuan argued that excessive yin force portended, as the "Treatise on the Five Phases" puts it, "subordinates conspiring against superiors," and urged tighter security in the palace and Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有挾刃犯謻門者。

translations.literal: Before long someone carrying a blade breached the Yi Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward an armed intruder breached the Yi Gate.

sentences.zh: 特賜五品服。

translations.literal: He was specially granted fifth-rank robes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor specially granted him fifth-rank robes in recognition.

sentences.zh: 又上疏曰：

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 農為國家急務，所以順天養財，御水旱，制蠻夷之原本也。

translations.literal: Agriculture is the urgent business of the state, by which to follow Heaven, nurture wealth, control floods and drought, and govern the root source of the Man and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Agriculture is the nation's most urgent concern—the means by which we align with Heaven, sustain the treasury, guard against flood and drought, and keep barbarian peoples in check at the source.

sentences.zh: 唐開元戶八百九十余萬，而墾田一千四百三十余萬頃。

translations.literal: In Tang's Kaiyuan era households numbered more than eight million nine hundred thousand, while reclaimed fields were more than fourteen million three hundred thousand qing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang Kaiyuan there were more than eight million nine hundred thousand households and more than fourteen million three hundred thousand qing under cultivation.

sentences.zh: 今國家戶七百三十余萬，而墾田二百一十五萬余頃，其間逃廢之田，不下三十余萬，是田疇不辟，而游手者多也。

translations.literal: Now the state's households are more than seven million three hundred thousand, while reclaimed fields are more than two million one hundred fifty thousand qing; among them abandoned fields are no less than three hundred thousand—thus fields are not opened, and idlers are many.
translations.idiomatic: Today the empire has more than seven million three hundred thousand households but only two million one hundred fifty thousand qing under cultivation—and at least three hundred thousand qing lie abandoned. Fields go untilled while idlers multiply.

sentences.zh: 勸課其可不興乎？

translations.literal: Can encouragement of cultivation not be raised up?
translations.idiomatic: Should not agricultural promotion be restored without delay?

sentences.zh: 本朝轉運使、提點刑獄、知州、通判，皆帶勸農之職，而徒有虛文，無勸導之實。

translations.literal: In our dynasty transport commissioners, judicial commissioners, prefects, and administrative prefects all carry the duty of encouraging agriculture, yet there are only empty documents and no reality of encouragement and guidance.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioners, judicial commissioners, prefects, and vice-prefects all bear the title of agricultural promoter, yet the duty exists only on paper.

sentences.zh: 宜置勸農司，以知州為長官，通判為佐，舉清強幕職、州縣官為判官。

translations.literal: It is fitting to establish an Agriculture Encouragement Office, with the prefect as chief, the administrative prefect as assistant, and select clear and forceful staff officials and county and prefecture officials as adjudicators.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed creating an Agriculture Promotion Office headed by the prefect, assisted by the vice-prefect, with capable staff and local officials as case officers.

sentences.zh: 先以墾田頃畝及戶口數、屋塘、山澤、溝洫、桑柘，著之於籍，然後設法勸課，除害興利。

translations.literal: First record in registers the qing and mu of reclaimed fields and household counts, houses and ponds, mountains and marshes, ditches and irrigation, mulberry and paper-mulberry; then establish methods to encourage cultivation, eliminate harm and raise profit.
translations.idiomatic: First register every qing and mu under cultivation, household counts, dwellings and ponds, hills and marshes, irrigation works, and mulberry groves—then promote farming through concrete measures to remove evils and create benefit.

sentences.zh: 歲終農隙，轉運司考校之，第其賞罰。

translations.literal: At year-end in the agricultural slack season, the transport commission should examine and verify, ranking rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end, during the farming slack season, transport commissioners should audit results and assign rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 楊懷敏妄言契丹主宗真死，乃除入內副都知；

translations.literal: Yang Huaimin falsely said the Khitan ruler Zongzhen was dead, yet was appointed Deputy Director of the Inner Service;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huaimin had falsely announced the death of the Khitan emperor Zongzhen, yet was promoted to Deputy Director of the Inner Service;

sentences.zh: 內侍黎用信以罪竄海島，赦歸，遽得環衛官致仕；

translations.literal: the inner attendant Li Yongxin was banished to a sea island for a crime, pardoned and returned, and abruptly received an Imperial Guard post leading to retirement;
translations.idiomatic: the inner attendant Li Yongxin, exiled to a distant island for a crime, was pardoned and immediately given an Imperial Guard appointment before retiring;

sentences.zh: 許懷德、慎鏞高年未謝事；

translations.literal: Xu Huaide and Shen Yong were advanced in years yet had not resigned office;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huaide and Shen Yong were elderly yet still held office;

sentences.zh: 楊景宗、郭承祐闟冗小人，宜廢不用：歷舉劾之，多見聽納。

translations.literal: Yang Jingzong and Guo Chengyou were trifling and superfluous petty men who should be discarded and not employed—he repeatedly memorialized and impeached them, and many of his points were heard and adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jingzong and Guo Chenyou were useless petty men who ought to be dismissed—Yanyuan impeached them repeatedly, and the court often heeded his counsel.

sentences.zh: 彥遠性豪邁，其任言職，數有建明。

translations.literal: Yanyuan by nature was bold and far-reaching; in his office of speaking out he often had constructive proposals.
translations.idiomatic: Bold by nature, Yanyuan made numerous constructive proposals during his tenure as remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 易子 明逸

translations.literal: Yi's son Mingyi
translations.idiomatic: Yi's son Mingyi

sentences.zh: 明逸字子飛。

translations.literal: Mingyi styled himself Zifei.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyi, styled Zifei.

sentences.zh: 繇殿中丞策制科，轉太常博士。

translations.literal: Starting from Palace Aide he entered the policy-examination category, and was transferred to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a Palace Aide, he passed the policy examination and was made Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 為呂夷簡所知，擢右正言。

translations.literal: Known by Lü Yijian, he was elevated to Right Rectifier of Deportment.
translations.idiomatic: Noticed by Grand Councilor Lü Yijian, he was promoted to Right Rectifier of Deportment.

sentences.zh: 首劾范仲淹、富弼：「更張綱紀，紛擾國經。

translations.literal: First he impeached Fan Zhongyan and Fu Bi: "They have changed and stretched the code and statutes, disturbing the foundations of state.
translations.idiomatic: He opened by impeaching Fan Zhongyan and Fu Bi: "They have overturned established institutions and thrown the foundations of state into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 凡所推薦，多挾朋黨。

translations.literal: All those they have recommended mostly carry factional ties.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly everyone they have advanced belongs to their faction.

sentences.zh: 乞早罷免，使奸詐不敢效尤，忠實得以自立。」

translations.literal: I beg that they be dismissed early, so that the crafty and deceitful dare not take them as examples, and the loyal and honest may stand on their own."
translations.idiomatic: I urge their immediate removal, so that the wicked dare not follow their example and honest men may hold their ground."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，二人皆罷；

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, both men were dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was delivered and both men were dismissed;

sentences.zh: 其夕，杜衍亦免相。

translations.literal: that same evening Du Yan was also removed as chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: that very evening Chief Councilor Du Yan was dismissed as well.

sentences.zh: 明逸蓋希章得象、陳執中意也。

translations.literal: Mingyi presumably hoped to win the approval of Zhang Dexiang and Chen Zhongyong.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyi was plainly courting the favor of Zhang Dexiang and Chen Zhongyong.

sentences.zh: 石元孫與夏人戰沒，以死事褒贈，既而生歸，朝廷釋不問。

translations.literal: Shi Yuansun died in battle with the Western Xia and was honored and posthumously enfeoffed for dying in service; afterward he returned alive, and the court released the matter without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yuansun was reported killed fighting the Western Xia and honored posthumously for dying in service—then turned up alive, and the court let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 明逸請正其僨軍之罪，乃竄之遠方而奪其恩。

translations.literal: Mingyi requested that his crime of desertion be corrected; he was then exiled to a distant place and stripped of the honors.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyi demanded that the crime of desertion be formally judged; Shi was banished to a distant posting and stripped of his honors.

sentences.zh: 進同修起居注、知制誥，擢知諫院，為翰林學士。

translations.literal: Advanced to Compiler of the Diary and Drafting Proclamations, elevated to head the Remonstrance Bureau, made Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Compiler of the Diary and Drafting Proclamations, made head of the Remonstrance Bureau, and appointed Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 自登科至是，才五年。

translations.literal: From passing the examination to this point was only five years.
translations.idiomatic: Only five years had passed since he first passed the examinations.

sentences.zh: 加史館修撰、知開封府。

translations.literal: Given the additional posts of Historiography Compiler and prefect of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Historiography Compiler and prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 妄人冷青自稱皇子，捕至府，明逸方正坐，青七曰：「明逸安得不起？」

translations.literal: A deluded man Leng Qing claimed to be the imperial prince; captured and brought to the prefecture, while Mingyi sat upright at his desk, Qing shouted: "How can Mingyi not rise?"
translations.idiomatic: A madman named Leng Qing claimed to be the emperor's son. When he was brought to the prefectural yamen, Mingyi was sitting upright at his desk. Leng Qing shouted at him, "Mingyi! How dare you not stand?"

sentences.zh: 明逸為起，坐尹京無威望；

translations.literal: Mingyi rose for him; he was blamed for presiding over the capital without authority;
translations.idiomatic: Mingyi stood up for him—a failure of authority as chief magistrate of the capital;

sentences.zh: 又獄吏榜婦人酇氏墮足死，罷為龍圖閣學士、知蔡州。

translations.literal: further, jailers beat the woman of the Zuo clan with cudgels until she fell and her foot broke and she died; he was dismissed to Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: and when jailers beat a detainee, Lady Zuo, until she fell and broke her foot and died, he was demoted to Dragon Diagram Hall Academician and prefect of Cai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歷揚、青、鄆、曹州、應天府，還，判流內銓、知通進銀台司，復出知成德軍、渭州。

translations.literal: He served successively at Yang, Qing, Yan, and Cao prefectures and Yingtian Prefecture; returning, he judged the Flowing Within Board and directed the Silver Terrace Office for Incoming Memorials; again sent out as military commissioner of Chengde Army and prefect of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively at Yangzhou, Qingzhou, Yanzhou, Caozhou, and Yingtian Prefecture. Recalled to court, he presided over the Flowing Within Board and directed the Silver Terrace Office. He was then sent out again as military commissioner of Chengde and prefect of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 加端明殿學士、知秦州。

translations.literal: Given the additional title Academician of the Duane Hall and appointed prefect of Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Duane Hall Academician and prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，于闐入貢，道邈川，唃廝囉留不遣。

translations.literal: Earlier, Khotan came to offer tribute; passing through Yaozhou, Gusiluo detained and did not release them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Khotan sent tribute, its envoys passed through Yaozhou and were detained by Gusiluo, who refused to let them proceed.

sentences.zh: 會其妻亡，前帥張方平請因而恤之，且誘其般次入貢，詔賻絹千匹。

translations.literal: It happened that his wife died; the former commander Zhang Fangping asked to console him on that occasion and also induce his tribute missions to come pay tribute; an edict granted condolence silk of one thousand bolts.
translations.idiomatic: When Gusiluo's wife died, the former frontier commander Zhang Fangping urged the court to offer condolences and coax his tribute missions back to court. An imperial edict granted one thousand bolts of condolence silk.

sentences.zh: 明逸言：「朝廷撫唃氏至厚，頃以招馬為名，賂繒縕；

translations.literal: Mingyi said: "The court's kindness toward the Gusiluo clan has been exceedingly generous; recently, under the pretext of recruiting horses, it has bribed them with silk;
translations.idiomatic: Mingyi argued: "The court has treated the Gusiluo clan with extraordinary generosity—lately bribing them with silk under the pretext of recruiting horses;

sentences.zh: 邀請六事，既徇其五，而猶觖望。

translations.literal: they requested six things, and though five were already granted, they were still discontent.
translations.idiomatic: they demanded six concessions, and though the court had already yielded on five, they remained dissatisfied.

sentences.zh: 今壅遏荒服之貢，固有罪矣，豈可復加賜以辱國體？」

translations.literal: Now to block tribute from the remote frontier is already a crime—how can we add further gifts and insult the dignity of the state?"
translations.idiomatic: Blocking tribute from the frontier is crime enough—how can we heap further gifts upon them and disgrace the realm?"

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 而于闐使與般次亦皆至。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Khotan envoys and the tribute missions all arrived as well.
translations.idiomatic: Khotan's envoys and the detained tribute missions all arrived.

sentences.zh: 廝囉有子質於秦，別子木征居河州。

translations.literal: Gusiluo had a son held as hostage at Qin Prefecture; another son, Muzheng, lived at He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gusiluo had one son held hostage at Qinzhou; another son, Muzheng, resided at Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 殿侍程從簡私與之盟，令過洮河，許以官，且歸其質子。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Cheng Congjian privately made a pact with him, telling him to cross the Tao River, promising him office and the return of his hostage son.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Cheng Congjian secretly entered an alliance with Muzheng, urging him to cross the Tao River and promising him an official post and the return of his hostage son.

sentences.zh: 事不驗，木征怒，留貢使。

translations.literal: When the matter did not materialize, Muzheng was enraged and detained the tribute envoys.
translations.idiomatic: When the promise failed to materialize, Muzheng flew into a rage and held the tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 明逸械從簡往詰，因斬之。

translations.literal: Mingyi shackled Congjian and went to interrogate him, then executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyi had Congjian shackled, went to confront him, and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 木征惶懼，悉遣所留者。

translations.literal: Muzheng, fearful, released all those he had detained.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Muzheng released every envoy he had held.

sentences.zh: 治平初，復為翰林學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhiping era he was again made Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhiping reign he was restored to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，御史論其傾險憸薄，頃附賈昌朝、夏竦以陷正人，文辭淺繆，豈應冒居翰院？

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong took the throne, censors charged that he was scheming, malicious, and petty, that he had recently attached himself to Jia Changchao and Xia Song to ruin upright men, and that his literary style was shallow and erroneous—how could he presume to occupy the Hanlin Academy?
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong ascended the throne, censors accused him of being scheming, malicious, and petty; of having lately joined Jia Changchao and Xia Song to destroy upright officials; and of writing in a shallow, slipshod style—unfit, they asked, for the Hanlin Academy?

sentences.zh: 乃罷學士。

translations.literal: He was therefore removed from the Hanlin post.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of his Hanlin appointment.

sentences.zh: 久之，知永興軍。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was made military commissioner of Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was appointed military commissioner of Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 熙寧四年，卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xining he died, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Xining, at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書，諡曰修懿。

translations.literal: Posthumously given Minister of Rites; his posthumous title was Xiuyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of Rites and given the posthumous title Xiuyi.

sentences.zh: 藻字醇老，明逸之從子也。

translations.literal: Zao, styled Chunlao, was Mingyi's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Zao, whose style name was Chunlao, was Mingyi's nephew.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，刻厲為學。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he applied himself strenuously to learning.
translations.idiomatic: Left fatherless young, he drove himself hard in his studies.

sentences.zh: 第進士，又中賢良方正科，為秘閣校理。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, also passed the Exemplary and Upright recruitment, and was made Secretariat Proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: He placed in the jinshi examination, also passed the Exemplary and Upright recruitment, and was appointed Secretariat Proofreader.

sentences.zh: 慈聖後臨朝，藻三上書乞還政。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Cisheng held the regency, Zao three times submitted memorials begging her to restore the government.
translations.idiomatic: While Empress Dowager Cisheng held the regency, Zao three times memorialized the throne, begging her to restore imperial rule.

sentences.zh: 同修起居注、知制誥。

translations.literal: He was made Co-Compiler of the Diary and Drafting Proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Co-Compiler of the Diary and Drafting Proclamations.

sentences.zh: 加樞密直學士、知開封府。

translations.literal: Given the additional posts of Privy Council Academician and prefect of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Privy Council Academician and prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 平居樂易無崖岸，而居官獨立守繩墨，為政簡靜有條理，不肯徇私取顯。

translations.literal: In daily life he was easygoing and without sharp edges, yet in office he stood alone in upholding the rules; his governance was simple, quiet, and orderly, and he would not favor connections to win renown.
translations.idiomatic: Affable and unpretentious in private life, in office he stood alone in upholding the law; his administration was spare, calm, and methodical, and he refused to trade favors for fame.

sentences.zh: 數求退，改翰林侍讀學士、知審官東院。

translations.literal: Repeatedly seeking retirement, he was changed to Hanlin Attendant Reader Academician and head of the Eastern Bureau of Appointments Review.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly sought to retire and was reassigned as Hanlin Attendant Reader Academician and head of the Eastern Bureau of Appointments Review.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 神宗知其貧，賻錢五十萬，贈太中大夫。

translations.literal: Shenzong knew he was poor and granted condolence money of five hundred thousand cash; posthumously given Grand Master of the Court.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he had died poor, Shenzong granted five hundred thousand cash in condolence gifts and posthumously made him Grand Master of the Court.

sentences.zh: 諸孫 景諶

translations.literal: Grandsons: Jingchen.
translations.idiomatic: Grandsons: Jingchen.

sentences.zh: 景諶，景臻之從兄也。

translations.literal: Jingchen was Jingzhen's elder cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchen was the elder cousin of Jingzhen.

sentences.zh: 繇殿直巡轄兩京馬遞，中進士第。

translations.literal: Starting as a Palace Attendant patrolling the horse-relay routes of both capitals, he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a Palace Attendant overseeing the horse-relay routes of both capitals, then passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 初赴開封解試，時王安石得其文，以為知道者。

translations.literal: When he first took the Kaifeng preliminary examination, Wang Anshi obtained his essay and regarded him as one who understood the Way.
translations.idiomatic: At his first Kaifeng preliminary examination, Wang Anshi read his essay and judged him a man who understood the Way.

sentences.zh: 既薦送之，又推譽於公卿間，自是執弟子禮。

translations.literal: After recommending him for advancement, he also praised him among ministers and grandees; from then on Jingchen performed the rites of a disciple.
translations.idiomatic: After sponsoring him for advancement, Anshi praised him among ministers and grandees, and from then on Jingchen treated him as his master.

sentences.zh: 安石提點府界，景諶為屬主簿，又以文薦之。

translations.literal: When Anshi was Intendant of the Capital Circuit, Jingchen served as his chief clerk, and Anshi again recommended him for his writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Anshi served as Intendant of the Capital Circuit, Jingchen was his chief clerk, and Anshi again recommended him for his literary talent.

sentences.zh: 執喪居許，聞安石得政，喜，因事來京師謁之。

translations.literal: Observing mourning at home in Xu, he heard that Anshi had come to power, rejoiced, and came to the capital on business to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: While observing mourning at home in Xu, he heard that Anshi had seized power, was delighted, and traveled to the capital on business to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 方盛夏，安石與僧智緣臥於地，一最親者袒坐其側。

translations.literal: It was high summer; Anshi lay on the ground with the monk Zhiyuan, while a most intimate companion sat bare-chested at his side.
translations.idiomatic: It was the height of summer. Anshi was sprawled on the floor with the monk Zhiyuan, a favorite companion sitting shirtless beside him.

sentences.zh: 顧景諶褫服脫帽，未及它語，卒然問曰：「青苗、助役如何？」

translations.literal: Seeing Jingchen remove his mourning dress and hat, before any other words were exchanged he suddenly asked: "How are the Green Sprouts and Labor Service policies?"
translations.idiomatic: Noticing Jingchen shed his mourning garb and cap, Anshi asked abruptly, before any other word was spoken: "What do you think of the Green Sprouts and Labor Service policies?"

sentences.zh: 景諶曰：「利少害多，異日必為民患。」

translations.literal: Jingchen said: "The benefit is slight and the harm great; someday they will surely become the people's affliction."
translations.idiomatic: Jingchen replied: "The benefit is slight and the harm great—they will surely become a scourge to the people."

sentences.zh: 又問：「孰為可用之人？」

translations.literal: He asked again: "Who are the men fit for use?"
translations.idiomatic: Anshi asked again: "Who, then, are the men worth employing?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「居喪不交人事，而知人尤難事也。」

translations.literal: He said: "I am in mourning and do not engage in worldly affairs; knowing men is an especially difficult matter."
translations.idiomatic: Jingchen answered: "I am in mourning and keep out of public affairs—judging men is the hardest thing of all."

sentences.zh: 遂辭出。

translations.literal: He then took his leave and departed.
translations.idiomatic: With that he bowed out and left.

sentences.zh: 後調官復來，安石已作相，又往詣之。

translations.literal: Later, after a transfer, he came again; Anshi was already chief councilor, and Jingchen again went to call on him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after a new appointment brought him back to the capital, Anshi was already chief councilor, and Jingchen visited him again.

sentences.zh: 安石令先與弟安國相見。

translations.literal: Anshi had him meet first with his younger brother Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi had him meet first with his younger brother Anguo.

sentences.zh: 安國亦與之善，謂景諶曰：「相君欲以館閣相處而任以事。」

translations.literal: Anguo was also on good terms with him and told Jingchen: "The Chancellor wishes to treat you as a palace archive member and entrust you with affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Anguo, who was also fond of him, said: "The Chancellor means to place you in the palace archives and charge you with real responsibilities."

sentences.zh: 景諶曰：「百事皆可為，所不知者新書、役法耳。」

translations.literal: Jingchen said: "Of a hundred affairs, all can be done; what I do not know are the New Policies books and the labor service law."
translations.idiomatic: Jingchen said: "I can undertake almost any task—what I cannot abide are the New Policies and the labor service law."

sentences.zh: 及見安石，安石欲令治峽路役書，且委以戎、滬蠻事。

translations.literal: When he saw Anshi, Anshi wanted him to compile the Gorges-route labor-service register and also entrusted him with the barbarian affairs of Rong and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: When he finally saw Anshi, the Chancellor wanted him to compile the Gorges-route labor-service register and also entrusted him with Rong and Lu frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 景諶曰：「峽路民情，僕固不能知；

translations.literal: Jingchen said: "The customs of the people along the Gorges route—I truly cannot know them;
translations.idiomatic: Jingchen said: "The temper of the people along the Gorges route is beyond my knowledge;

sentences.zh: 而戎、滬用兵，系朝廷舉動、一路生靈休戚，願擇知兵愛人者。」

translations.literal: but to deploy troops in Rong and Lu concerns the court's every move and the weal and woe of an entire circuit's people—I hope you will choose one who knows war and loves the people."
translations.idiomatic: but war in Rong and Lu touches the court's every move and the fate of a whole circuit's people. Choose someone who understands war and cherishes the people."

sentences.zh: 安石大怒，坐上客數十人，皆為之懼。

translations.literal: Anshi was greatly enraged; several dozen guests seated there all feared for Jingchen.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi flew into a rage. Several dozen guests present feared for Jingchen's life.

sentences.zh: 退就謁舍，賞激之與詆以為矯者參半。

translations.literal: When he withdrew to the guest quarters, those who praised and encouraged him and those who denounced him as affectation were evenly divided.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the guest quarters, opinion split evenly between those who admired his courage and those who dismissed it as posturing.

sentences.zh: 景諶笑曰：「自古以來，好利者眾，而顧義者寡，故天下萬事，皆由人而不在於己。

translations.literal: Jingchen smiled and said: "Since ancient times, those who seek profit have been many and those who heed righteousness few; thus all affairs under Heaven depend on others and not on oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchen smiled and said: "Since antiquity, profit-seekers have been legion and men of principle scarce—so the world's affairs turn on others, not on oneself.

sentences.zh: 苟為利所動，而由於人，則盜亦可為也。

translations.literal: If one is moved by profit and swayed by others, then even theft can be done.
translations.idiomatic: If profit moves you and others steer you, even theft becomes possible.

sentences.zh: 夫盜之所以為盜者，利勝於義，而不知所以為之者耳。

translations.literal: Thieves steal because profit overcomes righteousness, without knowing why they do it.
translations.idiomatic: Men steal because gain outweighs duty—they scarcely know why they act.

sentences.zh: 吾又何憾焉？」

translations.literal: What regret have I?"
translations.idiomatic: Why should I regret it?"

sentences.zh: 遂與安石絕。

translations.literal: He then broke with Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: He broke with Anshi for good.

sentences.zh: 熙寧末，從張景憲辟知瀛州，終身為外官，僅至朝請郎而卒。

translations.literal: Late in Xining he joined Zhang Jingxian's staff as prefect of Ying Prefecture; he spent his whole life as an outer official and at death had risen only to Gentleman for Palace Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Xining he entered Zhang Jingxian's staff as prefect of Yingzhou. He spent his career in provincial posts and died having risen no higher than Gentleman for Palace Attendance.

sentences.zh: 諸孫 勰

translations.literal: Grandsons: Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Grandsons: Xie.

sentences.zh: 勰字穆父，彥遠之子也。

translations.literal: Xie, styled Mufu, was Yanyuan's son.
translations.idiomatic: Xie, whose style name was Mufu, was the son of Yanyuan.

sentences.zh: 生五歲，日誦千言。

translations.literal: At five years of age he recited one thousand characters per day.
translations.idiomatic: At five he could recite a thousand characters each day.

sentences.zh: 十三歲，制舉之業成。

translations.literal: At thirteen he had mastered the work required for the Decree recruitment examination.
translations.idiomatic: By thirteen he had mastered the composition required for the Decree recruitment examination.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年試應，既中秘閣選，廷對入等矣，會王安石惡孔文仲策，遷怒罷其科，遂不得第。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xining he tested; he had already passed the Secretariat selection and entered the ranked tier in the palace debate, but Wang Anshi hated Kong Wenzhong's policy essay and, displacing his anger, abolished that category—thus Xie failed to place.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xining he sat for the examinations, passed the Secretariat selection, and entered the ranked tier in the palace debate—then Wang Anshi, enraged by Kong Wenzhong's policy essay, abolished the category in a fit of spite, and Xie failed to place.

sentences.zh: 以蔭知尉氏縣，授流內銓主簿。

translations.literal: By hereditary privilege he was made magistrate of Weishi County and appointed chief clerk of the Flowing Within Board.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he became magistrate of Weishi County and was appointed chief clerk of the Flowing Within Board.

sentences.zh: 判銓陳襄嘗登進班簿，神宗稱之。

translations.literal: Board judge Chen Xiang once presented the promotion roster; Shenzong praised it.
translations.idiomatic: When Board judge Chen Xiang once presented the promotion roster, Shenzong praised it.

sentences.zh: 襄曰：「此非臣所能，主薄錢勰為之耳。」

translations.literal: Xiang said: "This was not within my ability; Chief Clerk Qian Xie did it."
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said: "That was not my work—Chief Clerk Qian Xie prepared it."

sentences.zh: 明日召對，將任以清要官。

translations.literal: The next day Xie was summoned for audience; the emperor was about to appoint him to a prestigious office.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Xie was summoned to audience and was about to be given a prestigious appointment.

sentences.zh: 安石使弟安禮來見，許用為御史。

translations.literal: Anshi sent his younger brother Anli to see him and promised to appoint him censor.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi sent his brother Anli to visit him and offered to make him a censor.

sentences.zh: 勰謝曰：「家貧母老，不能為萬里行。」

translations.literal: Xie declined, saying: "My family is poor and my mother is old; I cannot undertake a journey of ten thousand li."
translations.idiomatic: Xie declined: "My family is poor and my mother is old—I cannot travel ten thousand li from home."

sentences.zh: 安石知不附己，命權鹽鐵判官，歷提點京西、河北、京東刑獄。

translations.literal: Anshi, knowing he would not attach himself, ordered him acting Salt and Iron Commissioner and had him serve successively as intendant of criminal justice for Jingxi, Hebei, and Jingdong.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Xie would not join him, Anshi assigned him acting Salt and Iron Commissioner and sent him successively as intendant of criminal justice for Jingxi, Hebei, and Jingdong.

sentences.zh: 元豐定官制，勰方居喪。

translations.literal: When the Yuanfeng official system was fixed, Xie was in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuanfeng reforms fixed the official system, Xie was observing mourning.

sentences.zh: 帝於左司郎中格自書其姓名，須終制日授之。

translations.literal: The emperor personally wrote his name in the Left Department Director grade and ordered that it be conferred when his mourning ended.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally wrote his name into the Left Department Director slot and ordered the appointment held until his mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 奉使吊高麗，外意頗謂欲結之以北伐。

translations.literal: Sent as envoy to offer condolences to Goryeo; outsiders largely supposed the court meant to ally with Goryeo for a northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatched to offer condolences to Goryeo, he was widely thought abroad to be forging an alliance for a northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 勰入請使指，帝曰：「高麗好文，又重士大夫家世，所以選卿，無他也。」

translations.literal: Xie entered and asked the purpose of the mission; the emperor said: "Goryeo loves literature and also values the family background of scholar-officials—that is why you were chosen, and for no other reason."
translations.idiomatic: Xie asked the emperor to clarify the mission. The emperor said: "Goryeo cherishes letters and respects a minister's pedigree—that is why I chose you, and for no other reason."

sentences.zh: 乃求呂端故事以行，凡饋餼非故所有者皆弗納。

translations.literal: He then sought the precedent of Lü Duan for his journey; all gifts and provisions not found in the old records he refused.
translations.idiomatic: He then took Lü Duan's embassy as his model; any gift or provision not authorized by precedent he refused.

sentences.zh: 歸次紫燕島，王遣二吏追餉金銀器四千兩。

translations.literal: On the return journey he stopped at Ziyan Island; the king sent two clerks after him with four thousand taels' worth of gold and silver vessels.
translations.idiomatic: On the homeward voyage he stopped at Ziyan Island, where the king sent two clerks after him bearing gold and silver vessels worth four thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 勰曰：「在館時既辭之矣，今何為者？」

translations.literal: Xie said: "I already refused them while at the embassy—what is this now?"
translations.idiomatic: Xie said: "I already refused these gifts at court—what is the meaning of this?"

sentences.zh: 吏泣曰：「王有命，徒歸則死，且左番已受。」

translations.literal: The clerk wept and said: "The king has ordered it; if I return empty-handed I die—and besides, the left clerk has already accepted."
translations.idiomatic: The clerk wept: "The king commands it. If I return empty-handed, I die—and the left clerk has already accepted his share."

sentences.zh: 勰曰：「左右番各有職，吾唯例是視，汝可死，吾不可受。」

translations.literal: Xie said: "The left and right clerks each have their duties; I look only to precedent—you may die, but I cannot accept."
translations.idiomatic: Xie said: "Left clerk and right clerk each have his duty. I follow precedent alone—you may die, but I will not take the gift."

sentences.zh: 竟卻之。

translations.literal: In the end he refused it.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to the end.

sentences.zh: 還，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was appointed Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，遷給事中，以龍圖閣待制知開封府。

translations.literal: Early in Yuanyou he was promoted to Supervising Censor and, as Dragon Diagram Hall Gentleman Serving, made prefect of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanyou he was promoted to Supervising Censor and, as Dragon Diagram Hall Gentleman Serving, appointed prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 老吏畏其敏，欲困以事，導人訴牒至七百。

translations.literal: Old clerks feared his sharpness and sought to overwhelm him with business, steering petitioners until the docket reached seven hundred cases.
translations.idiomatic: The veteran clerks feared his quick mind and tried to bury him in work, funneling petitions until seven hundred cases piled up.

sentences.zh: 勰隨即剖決，簡不中理者，緘而識之，戒無復來。

translations.literal: Xie immediately decided them; those he found unreasonable he sealed and marked, warning that they must not come again.
translations.idiomatic: Xie adjudicated them on the spot; cases he found meritless he sealed, marked, and warned never to bring again.

sentences.zh: 閱月聽訟，一人又至，呼詰之曰：「吾固戒汝矣，安得欺我？」

translations.literal: After a month of hearing cases, one man came again; Xie called and interrogated him, saying: "I already warned you—how dare you deceive me?"
translations.idiomatic: A month into hearing cases, one petitioner returned. Xie summoned and challenged him: "I warned you plainly—how dare you try to deceive me?"

sentences.zh: 其人讕曰：「無有。」

translations.literal: The man lied: "There was no such thing."
translations.idiomatic: The man lied: "Nothing of the kind happened."

sentences.zh: 勰曰：「汝前訴云云，吾識以某字。」

translations.literal: Xie said: "Your earlier petition ran thus and so—I marked it with a certain character."
translations.idiomatic: Xie said: "Your earlier petition said such and such—I marked it with a particular character."

sentences.zh: 啟緘示之，信然，上下皆驚吒。

translations.literal: He opened the seal and showed it; it was indeed so, and all above and below were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: He broke the seal and produced the document. It was exactly as he said, and everyone in the hall was stunned.

sentences.zh: 宗室、貴戚為之斂手，雖丞相府謁吏干請，亦械治之。

translations.literal: Members of the imperial clan and noble kin held themselves in check for him; even petition clerks from the chief councilor's yamen who sought favors were shackled and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen and noble kin learned to mind their manners; even lobbyists from the chief councilor's yamen were shackled and punished.

sentences.zh: 積為眾所憾，出知越州，徙瀛州。

translations.literal: He accumulated resentment from many quarters and was sent out as prefect of Yue Prefecture, then transferred to Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He made many enemies and was sent out as prefect of Yuezhou, then transferred to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 召拜工部、戶部侍郎，進尚書，加龍圖閣直學士，復知開封，臨事益精。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Works and Vice Minister of Revenue, promoted to Minister, given Dragon Diagram Hall Academician, again made prefect of Kaifeng, and in handling affairs grew ever more precise.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he was made Vice Minister of Works and Vice Minister of Revenue, then promoted to Minister, given Dragon Diagram Hall Academician, and again appointed prefect of Kaifeng, where his handling of affairs grew ever sharper.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾乘其據案時遺之詩，勰操筆立就以報。

translations.literal: Su Shi, while Xie leaned over his desk, sent him a poem; Xie took up the brush and immediately wrote a reply.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi sent him a poem while he sat at his desk; Xie seized the brush and answered on the spot.

sentences.zh: 軾曰：「電掃庭訟，響答詩筒，近所未見也。」

translations.literal: Su said: "Lightning in clearing court cases, an instant echo in the poetry tube—nothing like it has been seen in recent years."
translations.idiomatic: Su remarked: "Lightning through the court docket, an instant answer in the poetry tube—I have seen nothing like it in years."

sentences.zh: 哲宗蒞政，翰林缺學士，章惇三薦林希，帝以命勰，仍兼侍讀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong took the reins of government, the Hanlin Academy lacked an academician; Zhang Dun thrice recommended Lin Xi, but the emperor instead appointed Xie and also made him Attendant Reader.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong assumed personal rule, the Hanlin Academy had a vacancy; Zhang Dun recommended Lin Xi three times, but the emperor appointed Xie instead and also made him Attendant Reader.

sentences.zh: 以嘗行惇謫詞，懼而求去。

translations.literal: Because he had once drafted Dun's demotion edict, he feared Dun and sought to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Having once drafted Dun's demotion edict, he feared Dun and asked to be relieved.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「豈非『鞅鞅非少主之臣，硜硜無大臣之節』者乎？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Is this not the man of whom it was written, 'Sullen—not a servant of a young ruler; obstinate—without a great minister's integrity'?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Is this not the man described as 'sullen—not fit to serve a young ruler; obstinate—lacking a great minister's integrity'?

sentences.zh: 朕固知之，毋庸避也。」

translations.literal: I already know this; there is no need to avoid him."
translations.idiomatic: I know that already. You need not avoid him."

sentences.zh: 嘗侍經幄，帝留與之語曰：「台臣論徐邸事，其辭及鄭、雍，小人離間骨肉如此。

translations.literal: Once, while attending the scripture curtain, the emperor kept him to speak, saying: "Censors are debating the affair of Prince Xu's residence; their words touch on Zheng and Yong—petty men sunder flesh and blood like this.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while attending the scripture curtain, the emperor detained him and said: "The censorate is debating the affair of Prince Xu's residence, and their words implicate Zheng Yong—this is how petty men tear kin apart.

sentences.zh: 若雍有請，當付卿以美詔慰安之。」

translations.literal: If Yong submits a petition, you should be entrusted with a gracious edict to comfort him."
translations.idiomatic: If Yong submits a petition, I shall entrust you with a gracious edict to reassure him."

sentences.zh: 既而雍章至，勰答詔云：「弗容群枉，規欲動搖，朕察其厚誣，力加明辨，夫何異趣，乃爾乞身。」

translations.literal: Soon Yong's memorial arrived; Xie's reply edict read: "I will not tolerate a wicked faction scheming to shake the throne; I have examined their heavy slander and forcefully clarified the truth—what other intent could there be, that you thus beg to leave office?"
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yong's memorial arrived. Xie's reply edict ran: "I will not tolerate a wicked faction scheming to unsettle the throne. I have examined their gross slander and set the record straight—what other motive could you have in begging to leave office?"

sentences.zh: 帝見之，謂能道所欲言者。

translations.literal: When the emperor saw it, he said Xie was able to speak what he wished to say.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, reading it, said Xie could voice exactly what he himself wished to say.

sentences.zh: 惇因是極意排詆，諷全台攻之，言不已。

translations.literal: Dun therefore slandered him with all his might, inciting the whole censorate to attack him, and his words did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Dun then attacked him with all his venom, urging the entire censorate to assail him without letup.

sentences.zh: 罷知池州，卒於官，年六十四。

translations.literal: Dismissed to serve as prefect of Chi Prefecture, he died in office, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of office and sent out as prefect of Chizhou, he died in post at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 訃未至，帝猶即其從弟景臻問安否。

translations.literal: Before the death notice arrived, the emperor still asked his cousin Jingzhen how Xie was faring.
translations.idiomatic: Even before word of his death arrived, the emperor still asked his cousin Jingzhen after Xie's health.

sentences.zh: 元符末，追復龍圖閣學士。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuanfu era he was posthumously restored as Dragon Diagram Hall academician.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the Yuanfu period his Dragon Diagram Hall academician title was posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 諸孫 即

translations.literal: Grandson: Ji
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Ji

sentences.zh: 即字中道，吳越王諸孫也。

translations.literal: Ji, styled Zhongdao, was a grandson of the King of Wuyue.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, whose style name was Zhongdao, was a descendant of the King of Wuyue.

sentences.zh: 第進士，為睦州推官。

translations.literal: He ranked as jinshi and served as pushan of Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served as investigating officer in Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 部使者有獄在衢，啖即以薦牘，使往治。

translations.literal: A circuit commissioner had a case at Quzhou and tried to entice Ji with a recommendation letter to send him to handle it.
translations.idiomatic: A circuit intendant had a case at Quzhou and tried to bribe Ji with a recommendation to take it on.

sentences.zh: 即曰：「吾寧老冗選中，豈忍以數十人易一薦乎？」

translations.literal: Ji said: "I would rather grow old being picked for dead-end posts—how could I bear to trade dozens of lives for one recommendation?"
translations.idiomatic: Ji replied, "I would rather spend my years in obscure appointments than trade dozens of innocent lives for a single recommendation."

sentences.zh: 至，則平反之。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he reversed the wrongful verdict.
translations.idiomatic: Once there, he overturned the unjust conviction.

sentences.zh: 辟鄜延幕府。

translations.literal: He was recruited to the Fuyan military staff.
translations.idiomatic: He was invited onto the Fuyan circuit military staff.

sentences.zh: 崇寧中，為陝西轉運判官。

translations.literal: During the Chongning era he was transport judge of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongning he served as transport judge on the Shaanxi circuit.

sentences.zh: 王師復銀州，轉餉最。

translations.literal: When imperial forces recovered Yinzhou, his grain transport was rated the best.
translations.idiomatic: When the court retook Yinzhou, his supply convoys ranked first.

sentences.zh: 徽宗召對，問曰：「靈武可取乎？」

translations.literal: Huizong summoned him for audience and asked: "Can Lingwu be taken?"
translations.idiomatic: Huizong called him to court and asked, "Can we seize Lingwu?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「夏人去來飄忽，不能持久，是其所短；

translations.literal: He replied: "The Xia come and go swiftly and cannot endure long—that is their weakness;
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "The Tangut strike and withdraw—they cannot sustain a campaign. That is their weakness;

sentences.zh: 然其民皆兵，居不縻飲食，動不勤轉餉，願敕邊臣先為不可勝以待釁，庶可得志。」

translations.literal: yet their people are all soldiers; at rest they are not tied down by provisioning, and on campaign they do not strain to move grain supplies. I hope Your Majesty will instruct frontier officials first to make themselves unconquerable and await an opening—then you may achieve your aim."
translations.idiomatic: but every man is a soldier, they travel light, and they do not depend on supply trains. I urge Your Majesty to order the border commanders to make themselves unassailable first and wait for an opening—only then can you succeed."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：：「大砦泉可取否？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Can Dazhai Spring be taken?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Can we take Dazhai Spring?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「是所謂瀚海也。

translations.literal: He replied: "That is what is called the vast salt sea.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "That is the region known as the Vast Salt Sea.

sentences.zh: 臣聞其地皆舄鹵，無水泉，或以飲馬，口鼻皆裂，正得之無所用。」

translations.literal: I have heard the whole region is alkaline brine without springs; if one uses it to water horses, muzzle and lips all crack—even if taken it is useless."
translations.idiomatic: I am told the ground is all alkaline salt flats without fresh water; water horses there and their mouths crack open. Even if we took it, it would be worthless."

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 除直龍圖閣、知慶州。

translations.literal: He was appointed attached to the Dragon Diagram Hall and made prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made attached academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，築安邊城，歸德堡，包地萬頃，縱耕其中，歲得粟數十萬。

translations.literal: On reaching his post he built Pacify-the-Border city and Guide-to-Virtue fort, enclosing ten thousand qing of land and allowing free cultivation within—each year yielding several hundred thousand bushels of grain.
translations.idiomatic: At his post he built Pacify-the-Border city and Guide-to-Virtue fort, ringed ten thousand qing of land, and opened it to farming, harvesting several hundred thousand bushels of grain each year.

sentences.zh: 徙知延安府，加集賢殿修撰，又進徽猷閣待制、顯謨閣直學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Yan'an prefecture, made collator of the Hall of Assembled Talents, and advanced to awaiting draft in the Hall of Splendid Teachings and academician ex officio of the Hall of Manifest Purpose.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Yan'an, made collator of the Hall of Assembled Talents, and promoted to awaiting draft in the Hall of Splendid Teachings and academician ex officio of the Hall of Manifest Purpose.

sentences.zh: 在延五年，童貫宣撫陝西，得便宜行事。

translations.literal: For five years at Yan'an, Tong Guan pacified Shaanxi with discretionary authority.
translations.idiomatic: He spent five years at Yan'an while Tong Guan pacified Shaanxi with full discretionary powers.

sentences.zh: 時長安百物踴貴，錢幣益輕，貫欲力平之，計司承望風旨，取市價率減什四，違者重置於法，民至罷市。

translations.literal: At the time prices in Chang'an soared and money grew lighter; Guan wanted forcibly to stabilize them; the fiscal offices catered to his intent and cut market prices on average by forty percent—violators were heavily penalized until the people stopped trading altogether.
translations.idiomatic: Prices in Chang'an were soaring and coin was debased; Guan tried to force prices down. The fiscal offices followed his lead, slashing market prices by forty percent on average and punishing violators harshly until merchants shut their stalls.

sentences.zh: 徐處仁爭之，得罪。

translations.literal: Xu Churen protested and was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Churen objected and was punished for it.

sentences.zh: 又行均糴法，賤入民粟，而高金帛估以賞，下至蕃兵、射士之授田者，咸被抑配，關內騷然，幾於生變。

translations.literal: They also implemented equitable purchase—buying grain cheap from the people and rewarding with gold and silk at inflated valuations—down to tribal soldiers and archers holding allotted fields, all were forcibly assessed; the interior was in uproar and near revolt.
translations.idiomatic: They also imposed equitable purchase, buying grain cheap from the populace while valuing gold and silk rewards high. Even tribal soldiers and archers on allotted fields were forcibly assessed; the interior seethed and nearly erupted.

sentences.zh: 即亦屢抗章，極陳其害，貶永州團練副使，然糴害亦寢。

translations.literal: Ji also repeatedly memorialized in protest, detailing the harm, and was demoted to vice military training commissioner of Yongzhou; yet the purchase harm also ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Ji memorialized repeatedly against the policy, describing its damage in full, and was demoted to vice military training commissioner of Yongzhou, though the purchase scheme was also abandoned.

sentences.zh: 數月，還待制、知興仁府，從太原，以童貫宣撫本道辭，不許。

translations.literal: Several months later he was restored as awaiting draft and prefect of Xingren; he followed the Taiyuan campaign and pleaded illness citing Tong Guan's pacification of the circuit—his request was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Months later he was restored as awaiting draft and made prefect of Xingren. He joined the Taiyuan campaign and asked to be excused because Tong Guan was pacifying the circuit; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 居二年，以疾提舉洞霄宮，復真學士。

translations.literal: After two years, on grounds of illness he was made administrator of Dongxiao Palace and restored as true academician.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, citing illness, he was made administrator of Dongxiao Palace and restored as full academician.

sentences.zh: 睦寇作，起知宣州。

translations.literal: When the bandits of Muzhou rose, he was raised as prefect of Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Fang La rebels rose, he was recalled as prefect of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 即自力上道，至則悉意應軍須。

translations.literal: Ji exerted himself to set out on the road; on arrival he supplied the army's every need.
translations.idiomatic: Ji hurried to his post by his own effort and, once there, met every military need.

sentences.zh: 貫上其功，進龍圖閣學士。

translations.literal: Guan reported his merit and he was advanced to Dragon Diagram Hall academician.
translations.idiomatic: Guan reported his achievements and he was promoted to Dragon Diagram Hall academician.

sentences.zh: 貫遂引為河北、河東參謀，以老固辭，乃轉正奉大夫致仕。

translations.literal: Guan then wanted to bring him in as staff officer for Hebei and Hedong; he firmly declined on account of age and was made Senior Grand Master of the Faith with retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Guan then tried to appoint him staff officer for Hebei and Hedong, but he firmly declined on grounds of age and retired as Senior Grand Master of the Faith.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈金紫光祿大夫，諡曰忠定。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Golden Purple and posthumous name Zhongding.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Golden Purple with the posthumous name Loyal and Settling.

sentences.zh: 論曰：進士自鄉舉至廷試皆第一者才三人，王曾、宋庠為名宰相，馮京為名執政，風節相映，不愧其科名焉。

translations.literal: Commentary: Since the founding of the Song, only three men from the provincial examination through the Ministry and palace examinations ranked first at every stage—Wang Zeng and Song Qi were famous chief councilors, Feng Jing a famous executive—their moral stature reflected one another, not unworthy of their examination laurels.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Only three men since the Song founding placed first at every stage from the provincial exam through the palace test—Wang Zeng and Song Qi became renowned chief councilors, Feng Jing a renowned executive. Their integrity matched their fame, and they did honor to their degrees.

sentences.zh: 邵亢知太常，裁損張貴妃恤典，潁王授室、公主下嫁，請用古典，可謂不愧其官守矣。

translations.literal: Shao Kang understood the Directorate of Rituals, trimmed the mourning rites for Consort Zhang, and when the Prince of Ying took a wife and princesses married down requested ancient rites—he may be said not to have disgraced his office.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Kang mastered ritual affairs, scaled back Consort Zhang's mourning honors, and urged ancient ceremonies when the Prince of Ying married and when princesses wed commoners—he did not betray his office.

sentences.zh: 邵必亦習禮者也，預修《唐書》而能力辭，以為史出眾手，非古人撰述之體，豈非名言乎？

translations.literal: Shao Bi also studied ritual; though he took part in compiling the Book of Tang he could forcefully decline, holding that history produced by many hands was not the manner of ancient authorship—is this not a famous saying?
translations.idiomatic: Shao Bi likewise mastered ritual. Though invited to help compile the Book of Tang, he refused on the ground that history written by committee was not how the ancients composed—is that not a remark worth remembering?

sentences.zh: 錢惟演敏思清才，著稱當時，然急於柄用，阿附希進，遂喪名節。

translations.literal: Qian Weiyan was quick-minded with refined talent, renowned in his day, yet eager to wield power, fawning and hoping for advancement, and so lost his reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Weiyan was brilliant and polished, celebrated in his time, yet so eager for power that he fawned and schemed for promotion—and forfeited his good name.

sentences.zh: 錢氏三世制科，易、明逸皆掌書命，時人榮之。

translations.literal: Three generations of the Qian clan passed the specialized decree examinations; Yi and Mingyi both held charge of edict drafting—the age honored them.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations of the Qian family passed the special decree examinations; Yi and Mingyi both drafted imperial edicts, to the envy of their contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 惜乎易以輕俊，明逸以傾。

translations.literal: A pity that Yi was frivolous and Mingyi partisan.
translations.idiomatic: It is a pity that Yi was too flippant and Mingyi too partisan.
